tasks.context:
ROOT CAUSE: `~/.claude/tasks-config.json` holds a SINGLE `active_epic` value globally. When sessions span multiple repos (clients/*, ventures/*, thebrana), the focus bleeds — brana in client A reads the epic you last set in client B. `backlog_focus` and `brana backlog focus` both derive from this global, so focus/session routing is incoherent across repos.

DIRECTION: the CLI already knows the git root (`require_project_root()` pattern in brana-cli). `active_epic` (and optionally other per-project settings) should be keyed by the canonical git root path, not global. Possible shapes:

Option A — per-project section in the same file:
  {"active_epic": null, "projects": {"/path/to/thebrana": {"active_epic": "harness"}, "/path/to/client-a": {"active_epic": "onboarding"}}}
  `backlog_focus` reads from `.projects[git_root].active_epic`, falls back to global `active_epic`.

Option B — per-project config file at `.claude/tasks-config.json` INSIDE the repo (gitignored):
  Each repo carries its own focus. CLI reads the nearest `.claude/tasks-config.json` up the tree (same pattern as CLAUDE.md resolution). Simpler — no path-keyed map.

RELATED: t-2152 (session handoff routing by unit key) — the same blast radius: a global pointer causes cross-repo contamination. The two fixes compose: focus determines the SESSION's unit key; session write uses that key for routing. Coordinate.

CONSTRAINT: `brana backlog set-active` and MCP `backlog_set` need to write to the scoped location, not clobber the global. Migration: existing global `active_epic` stays as the default when no per-project value is set.

tasks.description: The autonomous runner's safety story rests on git-worktree isolation + human review of runner/auto/* branches. A native hive-mind workflow (t-2167 prompt 6) identified the riskiest assumption: a git worktree isolates tracked files in a checkout, NOT the OS process. The runner dispatches `claude -p --allowedTools "Read,Write,Edit,Bash"` (autonomous-runner.sh ~line 198) with Bash unscoped — no --sandbox, no disallowedTools, no egress block. Every downstream gate (git status --porcelain, validate, git add -A, human diff review) only inspects the worktree's tracked diff, so any side effect that never lands as a tracked file — network egress, writes to $HOME, reads of ~/.config/brana/*.env secrets, rm, package installs, git push — is invisible to all gates and to the reviewer. Containment must live at the capability layer, not the git layer.

1. bwrap 0.11.1 has NO --rlimit-nproc/--rlimit-fsize flags → apply rlimits via inner `bash -c 'ulimit -u N; exec ...'` (or prlimit).
2. claude is a 222MB ELF at ~/.local/share/claude/versions/<v>; ~/.local/bin/claude is a symlink. Must --ro-bind the RESOLVED binary (readlink -f) to e.g. /opt/claude; ~/.local is not otherwise bound.

4. claude needs a WRITABLE HOME: --tmpfs /home + env HOME=/home/sb + --ro-bind real creds to /home/sb/.claude/.credentials.json (bind after tmpfs auto-creates parent). F2 fix confirmed: doc's HOME=/tmp + creds at $HOME/.claude mismatch would fail auth.
5. Pass </dev/null to claude -p (else 3s stdin wait warning).

tasks.description: When Claude generates questions (gaps, doubts, owed info, errors), the answers/resolutions that later arrive often never make it back into the docs — they stay in chat. Result: (1) the source doc/spec stays stale, and (2) the unresolved questions linger in context and contaminate later reasoning. Need a designed mechanism: a centralized place to register open questions / awaiting-info items, and a flow that — when the answer or "the light" comes — removes the question and propagates/reconciles the new info into the right doc instead of just stating it in chat. Likely linked to the /brana:log command/skill (event handling) and to /brana:reconcile (propagation). User's tentative direction: remove the question and replace-and-propagate the incoming info that resolves it. This is a DISCUSS-AND-DESIGN task, not a build — open the design conversation before any implementation.

tasks.context:
2026-06-22: CONFIRMED LIVE — `sqlite3 ~/.swarm/memory.db 'PRAGMA quick_check'` => "database disk image is malformed (11)". journal_mode=wal. This is what broke session start today (memory search FAILED + 3 failed memory writes surfaced).

CAUSAL LINK (strong): t-2085 (2026-06-14) removed the flock mutex AND orphan-sweep from ruflo-mcp.sh on the explicit assumption "SQLite WAL serializes concurrent writes safely" (see field-note ruflo-multi-session-flock-removal). That assumption is incomplete: WAL prevents writer interleaving but does NOT protect against a writer being SIGKILL'd mid-checkpoint. Each CC session spawns its own `ruflo mcp start` stdio child; when CC tears the child down at session end (or on crash/compact), a kill during WAL checkpoint corrupts the DB. More parallel sessions = more checkpoint windows = matches user's "parallel sessions" gut and the "frequently" cadence.

Note: HTTP/daemon transport is NOT a viable single-writer fix — field-note ruflo-http-mode-theater confirms `ruflo mcp start -t http` is unimplemented theater (prints Running, never binds port). So a true single shared daemon isn't available via ruflo today.

1. Graceful shutdown in ruflo-mcp.sh / SessionEnd hook: SIGTERM + wait for clean exit (let WAL checkpoint finish) instead of abrupt kill. Likely the root fix.
2. PRAGMA synchronous=FULL + wal_autocheckpoint tuning to shrink the corruption window.
3. Single-writer serialization across sessions WITHOUT the broken orphan-sweep: advisory flock around write ops only (not a process mutex), or route all writes through one long-lived process.
4. Self-heal: SessionStart integrity check (PRAGMA quick_check) -> auto-restore newest ~/.swarm/backups/memory_*.db on corruption + alert. Backups exist (daily, newest memory_20260622.db).

IMMEDIATE UNBLOCK (separate from fix): restore memory.db from ~/.swarm/backups/memory_20260622.db (verify integrity first). Learning loop is down until then.

tasks.description:
gate-and-evidence.md Step 1b documents: `${SESSION_RANGE:+--git-range "$SESSION_RANGE"}` as a bare (unquoted-at-the-braces) shell expansion to conditionally pass --git-range. Verified empirically (2026-07-02 close) that bash does NOT split this into two argv words as expected — the nested double-quotes inside the :+ replacement word suppress field-splitting of the entire expansion, so it arrives at close-snapshot.sh as ONE argument: "--git-range 225c3b9d..ca098777" (literal embedded space), which the script's case statement rejects as "unknown argument". Every close that reaches Step 1b with a non-empty SESSION_RANGE hits this — silently degrades (close-snapshot exits 2, but per its own docs "close NEVER blocks on the queue" so the failure is swallowed and the session simply doesn't get queued for nightly extraction).

Fix: build an explicit bash array instead of the bare parameter-expansion idiom, e.g.:
ARGS=(--git-root "$GIT_ROOT" --branch "$BRANCH" --project "$PROJECT" --commit-count "$COMMIT_COUNT")
[ -n "$SESSION_RANGE" ] && ARGS+=(--git-range "$SESSION_RANGE")
bash close-snapshot.sh "${ARGS[@]}"

Verified this array form works correctly (tested live in the 2026-07-02 client-normalization close). Same fix needed anywhere else this idiom is copy-pasted (grep the codebase for `:+--git-range`).

tasks.description:
~/.swarm/memory.db (ruflo's SQLite memory store) has corrupted at the page level 3+ times: 2026-06-07, a 2026-06-16→06-28 cluster (fixed by t-2236's integrity gate), and a 2026-07-06→07-16 recurrence (fixed by t-2260, which closed the WAL-skip loophole in that same gate). Every fix so far has patched the detection/backup layer — integrity-gating backup-memory.sh and ruflo-mcp.sh — not the write path itself. Nothing explains how the pages actually get corrupted in the first place.

Leading suspect: 5 concurrent `ruflo mcp start` processes were observed running simultaneously on 2026-07-16, all writing to the same memory.db. ruflo-mcp.sh relies on SQLite WAL mode to serialize concurrent writers safely, and its own comments (citing t-2085) explicitly reject flock/orphan-sweep as having *caused* corruption previously — so the assumption that WAL mode alone is sufficient under this process topology hasn't been validated, and may be wrong.

Investigate:
- Whether concurrent `ruflo mcp start` processes (one per Claude Code session/window) are actually safe under SQLite WAL, or whether stale/orphaned processes are holding locks/partial transactions across crashes
- Whether ~/.swarm sits on a filesystem with fsync/mmap quirks relevant to SQLite's WAL durability guarantees
- Whether a specific ruflo memory-write code path (batch store, embeddings write, hive-mind/consolidation jobs) bypasses normal WAL-safe writes
- Whether corruption timing correlates with session crashes, machine sleep/resume, or specific ruflo commands
tasks.notes: REPORT: root cause identified with high confidence, independently corroborated by upstream (ruvnet/ruflo#2512 open PR citing their own ADR-100 R2a as P0, and #1257 closed issue with matching file:line detail). Missing PRAGMA busy_timeout in @claude-flow/memory's SQLiteBackend + memory-initializer.js, compounded by hybrid-backend.js's hardcoded dualWrite:true (concurrent sqlite+agentdb writes per store() call) and missing transaction wrapping around store()'s 3 statements. Confirmed our live topology: 5 concurrent ruflo mcp start processes, all with live parent claude sessions (not orphaned) -- ruled that hypothesis out. Ruled out filesystem/mmap quirks (plain ext4, zero kernel I/O errors in 30 days) and mixed journal modes (walMode:true always). Cannot fix directly -- defect is in vendored node_modules (third-party npm package), not this repo. Findings written to project_ruflo-memory-corruption-recurring memory per AC3. No follow-up task filed: our existing t-2236/t-2260 detection+recovery layer already covers the symptom with zero data loss; recommended path is tracking upstream #2512 for merge and upgrading ruflo.
tasks.subject: Investigate root cause of recurring ruflo memory.db page corruption

system/skills/close/phases/cleanup.md Step 11c (Pending-task reconcile) computes STALE via `for id in $PENDING_IDS; do ... done` with an unquoted multi-line variable. This is safe under bash (word-splits on whitespace/newlines) but silently broken under zsh (no word-splitting on unquoted expansion by default) — the whole $PENDING_IDS blob becomes a single loop iteration with $id equal to the entire newline-joined ID list, which gets embedded literally into the grep -E pattern and produces nonsense results.

This session's Bash tool actually runs zsh (`ps -p $$ -o comm=` → zsh), not bash, despite the tool's name — so this bug fires on every close in this environment.

Same class of bug already independently found and logged today in a different project as pattern_zsh-for-loop-no-word-split_2026-07-16.

tasks.description:
During a 2026-07-16 /brana:close --finish in thebrana, Step 9c's 4-tier epic-detection cascade (system/skills/close/phases/session-state.md) mis-attributed an unrelated session (ruflo memory.db repair, t-2260/t-2261) to the epic "orbit". Root cause chain:

1. t-2260 and t-2261 were created via the MCP backlog_add tool, whose schema has no "epic" parameter (only "tags") — so neither task ever got an epic field set, even though both were tagged "harness" and worked on branch harness/fix/t-2260-wal-integrity-gate.
2. Tier 2b (extract task IDs from recent commits, look up their epic field) came back empty because of gap #1.
3. Tier 2a (query in-progress tasks for a common epic) found exactly one non-empty result: "orbit", from t-2173 — a completely unrelated in-progress task from a different, concurrently active worktree (thebrana-orbit-t2173).
4. Per the protocol's mechanical "exactly 1 unique non-empty slug → use it silently, Done" rule, "orbit" was accepted as this session's epic with no cross-check against the actual work.
5. `brana session write` then routed the handoff by epic key to session-state-orbit.json — CLOBBERING the live, current state of the actively in-progress orbit/t-2173 lane with this session's unrelated content. The clobbered orbit content was recoverable from `brana session history` (last written 2026-06-22) and was manually restored in-session; had no history entry existed, or had the orbit lane written more recently via a path outside session_history, this would have been an unrecoverable data loss for a concurrent, still-active parallel session.

This is a structural gap: Tier 2a's "query in-progress tasks for a common epic" heuristic has no way to distinguish "this session's own in-progress task carries this epic" from "some other completely unrelated in-progress task happens to be the only one with a non-empty epic field." It also doesn't account for concurrent-session safety — clobbering another actively-worked lane's session-state file is a "same-day parallel close loses data" class of bug (see the close skill's own Field Notes, 2026-05-19 entry), just triggered through the epic key rather than the day key.

Two related, low-severity issues discovered during t-2263 (both out of scope for its ACs, confirmed independently by the Challenger gate during t-2263 review):

1. system/skills/close/phases/session-state.md Tier 2c extracts the branch slug via `git branch --show-current | sed "s|.*/||"`, which takes the text after the LAST slash. For this repo's actual 3-segment branch convention `{epic}/{type}/t-{N}-{slug}`, that yields the description-slug (e.g. t-2260-wal-integrity-gate), not the epic (e.g. harness). This contradicts the authoritative parser (session.rs epic_scoped_state_path's regex, which captures the FIRST segment as epic). Net effect: Tier 2c's "matches a known epic slug" check will almost never fire for a real branch, so it silently falls through to Tier 3 (ask) more often than the tier's own text implies it should. Fails safe (extra prompt, not silent-wrong) but is dead/misleading logic. Fix: change the sed to extract the FIRST segment, matching epic_scoped_state_path's regex.

2. system/cli/rust/crates/brana-cli/src/commands/run.rs (cmd_run, ~lines 48-49 and 57-58) passes a bare branch string to `git worktree add ... -b branch` / `git worktree add ... branch` with no refs/heads/ or -- protection — same anti-pattern class as the git log call fixed in session.rs::branch_has_active_worktree (t-2263). Currently NOT exploitable (branch always comes from tasks::branch_for_task, a fixed literal-prefix enum that never starts with -), but worth hardening for defense-in-depth consistency with the just-fixed call site.

tasks.description:
Two additive flags to backlog CLI so epic-scoped "what's ready now" and sorted mixed-status views are first-class, not ad-hoc Python.

Rethink active-epic scoping. Today a GLOBAL active_epic applies across every project, which is wrong — epics are project/client-scoped. Operator flagged 2026-07-20: "we can not have an active epic somewhere and applies everywhere."

Root bug — write/read path disconnect:
- `brana backlog set-active` (t-2155) writes PROJECT-LOCAL .claude/tasks-config.json.
- `backlog focus` and `backlog add` auto-assign READ the GLOBAL ~/.claude/tasks-config.json.
- Observed leak: thebrana has no project-local tasks-config.json → focus/add fall through to the global value `identity-commerce-rebuild` (a proyecto_anita commerce epic), applying a foreign epic to thebrana tasks.

Proposed direction (design decision, needs ADR): active_epic resolves PROJECT-LOCAL ONLY. If a project has not set one → no focus boost, and `add` asks for the epic rather than inheriting any global/foreign value. Remove or demote the global active_epic so it can never apply cross-project. Include migration for the existing global value + the two-copies sync issue (deployed ~/.claude vs repo copy, see pattern active-epic-two-copies).

Fold into the v3 backlog redesign — this is a gap the redesign doc does not yet cover.

tasks.context: 2026-07-22: Found during t-1999. brana-scheduler deploy iterates jobs alphabetically and generates a systemd timer per job via OnCalendar={{SCHEDULE}}. If ANY job has an unparseable schedule (e.g. knowledge-pipeline-tier1 had cron '0 3 * * *', invalid OnCalendar), the deploy loop aborts at that job — every alphabetically-later job silently never gets its timer created/updated. This is how reminder-dispatch's timer failed to deploy until the cron schedule was fixed. Fix: validate each schedule with `systemd-analyze calendar` before generating the unit; on failure, warn+skip that ONE job and continue (don't abort the whole deploy). Optionally add a validate.sh check that flags any job schedule that isn't valid OnCalendar. AC: one bad schedule does not prevent other jobs' timers from deploying; deploy reports the bad job clearly and exits non-zero only after processing all valid ones.

tasks.context:
Problem: @TheBranaBot is currently one-way — outbound reminder/notify dispatch only (ADR-054, t-1999). No way to interact with thebrana from the phone. Want to query/act on backlog + reminders + status without opening a terminal.

Design (ADR-002: thin layer over systemd, NO new daemons):
- Prefer POLLING getUpdates via a scheduler job (e.g. every 1-2 min) over webhook (needs public HTTPS endpoint) or long-poll (needs persistent process). Track update offset so each message is processed once (store last offset in ~/.claude/ state). This mirrors the reminder-dispatch job pattern (t-1999). Set noProjectLock:true (writes only its own state, never tasks.json).
- Owner-auth: accept commands ONLY from OWNER_CHAT_ID (~/.hub-secrets, currently 710037683); silently ignore all other chats. This is a control surface for brana CLI — untrusted input must be rejected.
- Reuse existing plumbing: ~/.hub-secrets (TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN + OWNER_CHAT_ID), brana notify send --channel telegram for replies, brana backlog/remind CLIs for actions.
- Command router: parse leading /command + args, dispatch to a handler, reply with formatted plain text (telegram adapter omits parse_mode — plain text only, ADR-054).

Suggested v1 commands: /help, /focus (brana backlog focus), /next, /tasks [status], /remind <text> [at HH:MM], /status (brana ops/backlog stats). Register the command list with BotFather so they autocomplete in the Telegram UI.

Security: command handlers exec brana CLI — never pass raw telegram text into a shell; use argv arrays. Rate-limit / dedupe by update_id. getUpdates conflicts with any webhook — ensure no webhook is set (deleteWebhook) if polling.

--- 2026-07-22 brainstorm update (docs/ideas/mcp-lock-timeout.md) ---
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (not inferred — verified via source):
1. brana-core/src/util.rs:774-787 lock_sidecar() calls f.lock() — synchronous blocking flock(2), NO timeout, called directly inside an async MCP tool handler.
2. pmcp 2.1.0's stdio dispatch is FULLY SERIALIZED (verified in ~/.cargo/registry/src/.../pmcp-2.1.0/src/server/mod.rs:744-765): spawn_message_handler is a single spawned task looping receive_message -> handle_transport_message(...).await -> loop; handle_request_message awaits server.handle_request(...) inline, no per-request tokio::spawn. Zero concurrency across requests by design.
Consequence: one handler blocked on unbounded flock() (contending with concurrent brana CLI writes) freezes the ENTIRE server for the rest of the session — every subsequent request of ANY tool queues behind it, including reads (backlog_get) that don't even take the lock. Explains why get/search/add all hung in sequence: one earlier stuck call starving pmcp's single loop, not 3 independent bugs.
RULED OUT: session_write's 78 historical tool-failures are a SEPARATE issue — session.rs confirmed NOT using lock_sidecar/flock at all (different write path: archive+validate+atomic-rename). Different symptom (fast error vs hang). Do not conflate.
CHALLENGED AND REJECTED: spawn_blocking alone is NOT sufficient — it frees other tokio tasks but pmcp's message loop still can't read the next request until the current handler's future resolves (linear dispatch). The lock acquire itself must be bounded.

CONCRETE FIX PLAN:
1. Add bounded lock-acquire (timeout + clear distinct error, e.g. 5-10s poll/retry on try_lock) to brana-core::util::lock_sidecar or a sibling fn used by MCP handlers.
2. Wrap lock acquire + read/write in spawn_blocking in MCP tool handlers (secondary hardening, doesn't fix core symptom alone but frees background tokio tasks).
3. Regression test: hold sidecar lock from one process/thread, confirm second acquire times out cleanly (bounded) instead of hanging — mirrors test-scheduler-runner-lock.sh pattern (t-2292, same session).
4. Reproduce end-to-end: hold lock, fire backlog_get via MCP path, confirm clean timeout error within window instead of hang.
RISK: bounded timeout could convert hang->retry-storm if callers don't back off — needs distinct error type + backoff-aware callers, tested under real concurrent-writer load not just single-process unit tests. Also add diagnostic (log PID/timestamp holding lock) for future debuggability.

tasks.description: brana-mcp tool handlers hang indefinitely under lock contention. Root cause (verified against source): lock_sidecar() in brana-core uses a synchronous, unbounded flock(2), and pmcp 2.1.0's stdio dispatch is fully serialized (no per-request concurrency) — so one blocked handler freezes the entire server, including unrelated read-only calls. Fix: add a bounded lock-acquire timeout with a distinct error type, wrap in spawn_blocking, and add a regression test. See docs/ideas/mcp-lock-timeout.md for full design.

Iteration 2: PROCEED WITH CHANGES (1 severity-3 finding: AC4/design-doc wording still asserted something now-proven-false about backlog_get itself -- corrected before close, non-blocking). Retrospective: root-caused via direct verification against vendored pmcp source (not docs/speculation) -- lock_sidecar()'s unbounded flock() + pmcp's fully-serialized (non-pipelined) stdio dispatch loop. tasks.context:
system/skills/close/phases/gate-and-evidence.md Step 1b documents: bash "$HOME/.claude/scripts/close-snapshot.sh" ... ${SESSION_RANGE:+--git-range "$SESSION_RANGE"} — this relies on the unquoted ${VAR:+...} expansion word-splitting into separate args. Under zsh (this environment's default shell — confirmed via $0 and ps -p $$ during a live close), unquoted parameter expansions do NOT word-split by default (no SH_WORD_SPLIT), so '--git-range c5c15bc2..ef628191' collapses into ONE argument and close-snapshot.sh errors 'unknown argument --git-range c5c15bc2..ef628191' — the snapshot silently fails to queue (script exits 2, but the phase doc has no error-checking around the call, so this could go unnoticed). Reproduced live in proyecto_anita 2026-07-23. Fix: wrap the call in bash -c with an explicit array, or restructure to always pass --git-range (never rely on conditional word-splitting), e.g.:

ARGS=(--git-root "..." --branch "..." --project "..." --commit-count "...")
[ -n "$SESSION_RANGE" ] && ARGS+=(--git-range "$SESSION_RANGE")

tasks.description:
Discovered during t-2325's CLOSE (2026-07-23): mcp__brana__backlog_set successfully wrote a flat `epic: "cli-backlog-schema"` value onto t-2325 mid-session, even though that field is sealed at set_field()'s whitelist level (t-2310, ADR-065) in the dev/feature-branch source. The live mcp__brana__* MCP server is a separately-deployed binary (last shipped to `main` via bootstrap.sh) — it doesn't pick up write-path sealing added on `dev`/feature branches until the next ship cycle. Root cause is structural: ADR-060's two-tier dev/main model means any session doing schema-migration work (retiring/sealing a field) is itself exposed to writing pre-migration-shape data back into the shared tasks.json via the still-live-old MCP tools, for the entire window between "sealing lands on dev" and "next ship to main". validate.sh Checks 63/64 catch it after the fact (which is how this was found — t-2325 and t-2377 both had stray epic keys post-merge), but nothing prevents the write or warns at write time.

Two fix directions worth deciding between: (a) process — ship schema-sealing changes to main faster/immediately after they merge to dev, shrinking the exposure window; (b) tooling — have the MCP server (or a wrapping hook) detect version skew against the source it should be enforcing and warn/refuse retired-field writes even from a stale binary, or auto-restart the MCP server after a relevant bootstrap.sh deploy. Needs a decision before implementation — filing as research/design, not a direct code task.
tasks.notes:
DECISION (2026-07-24): Both — narrow process exception + a small tooling fix shipped now; deeper tooling fix filed as follow-up (t-2385).

## Investigation findings

1. **Ship cadence (process)**: docs/guide/workflows/branching.md (ADR-060) explicitly frames "main lagging dev" as *the intended safety buffer*, not a problem to close eagerly — ship is a periodic, human-gated, batch action, not per-feature. Blanket "ship faster/more often" would undermine that design and add ship-cadence overhead for every change, most of which don't corrupt shared state when stale.

2. **Why schema-sealing is special**: unlike ordinary feature lag (stale binary = missing behavior, harmless), a stale MCP binary during schema-sealing can actively *write corrupted data* into the one shared, unversioned `tasks.json` that both dev-branch work and the live binary point at simultaneously. This is a shared-mutable-state hazard, not a normal feature-lag hazard, so it warrants an exception to the general "don't ship eagerly" policy — but only for this class of change.

3. **MCP binary versioning/build (tooling)**: `brana-mcp` (system/cli/rust/crates/brana-mcp) is a separate binary from `brana` (brana-cli), both built from the same Rust workspace, both installed manually to `~/.local/bin/`. bootstrap.sh step 7d already has a staleness-check pattern (`find *.rs -newer $BIN`) for `brana` — but it ONLY checked `brana`, never `brana-mcp`. Confirmed live: `brana` was rebuilt 2026-07-24 10:39 (this session's ship) while `brana-mcp` was still dated 2026-07-22 15:14 — i.e. bootstrap.sh's own freshness check had a blind spot for exactly the binary that caused this bug, even during a ship that was supposed to fix it.

4. **"Restart CC sessions after ship" mitigation**: real but incomplete. It fixes exposure *after* a ship (window B: ship landed, but resident MCP process hasn't reloaded) — necessary but was previously undiscoverable without inspecting binary mtimes by hand, since nothing told you the binary was stale. It does NOT touch the exposure that actually caused all 3 incidents (window A: sealing change merged to dev, but hasn't shipped to main yet — the live binary predates the change entirely, by design, per ADR-060's buffer).

## Recommendation

- **Process (narrow, not blanket)**: schema-sealing/retired-field commits should be called out as an explicit exception to the normal "ship in batches" cadence — fast-track just that commit to main+bootstrap+restart rather than waiting for a batch. This is a documentation/practice note, not a mechanism; no code change needed for this part. (Left as a practice reminder here rather than editing branching.md, to avoid overclaiming a repo-wide policy change beyond this task's S scope — worth a follow-up docs edit if this recurs again.)
- **Tooling (shipped now, trivial)**: extended bootstrap.sh's existing step-7d staleness-check pattern to also cover `brana-mcp` (previously unchecked) — mirrors the existing brana-cli check, ~16 lines, no new mechanism. Commit e729703a on branch `deploy-lag/research/t-2378-mcp-schema-skew`, merged to `dev` at 1b1b95b8. This closes visibility into window B (post-ship staleness) but not window A (pre-ship).
- **Tooling (deferred, follow-up filed as t-2385, M effort)**: a write-time guard in brana-core — a compiled-in `RETIRED_FIELDS` constant checked on every write path (mirroring t-2310's field whitelist), hard-refusing writes of sealed fields regardless of which binary/process version is running. Design sketch is in t-2385's context. This is the mechanism that actually prevents regression once a binary has shipped a sealing change; it does not (cannot) shrink window A, since a binary built before a field is retired can't know to reject it — only the fast-tracked-ship exception above addresses window A.

## Why not a general schema-version marker
Considered and rejected (documented in t-2385): a semver/marker-file skew-detection system adds a second artifact to keep in sync without preventing more than the simpler retired-field constant does — every incident so far was "old binary still recognizes a since-retired field," never a subtler format-skew case that would need a general version comparison.

Follow-up: t-2385 (M, write-time RETIRED_FIELDS guard).

tasks.context:
AC: root cause identified (write-path atomicity vs read-path locking)\nAC: fix implemented (atomic write+rename and/or read-side lock/retry) OR reasoned decision to accept the risk documented\nAC: no regression in brana backlog get/query performance under normal (non-concurrent) use\nSource: t-2375 close session, 2026-07-24 — reproduced 4+ times live
2026-07-24: reproduced again during t-2377's close, Step 9c epic-ancestor-walk — several `brana backlog get {id}` calls in a loop hit "Invalid string: control characters ... must be escaped" jq parse errors while another session's writes were presumably in flight. 5th+ live reproduction. resolve_epic_ancestor()'s existing fail-open ("" on parse failure) degraded gracefully as designed — no incorrect result, just a dropped signal.
2026-07-24: related but distinct failure mode observed (not JSON corruption, a semantic collision) - two concurrent sessions independently investigated and closed the SAME task (t-2378) with different decisions, different branches, and different follow-up tasks (t-2384 vs t-2385) written via field-level backlog_set calls. No JSON corruption occurred (field-level writes merged cleanly, first-committer's fields preserved, second session's fields layered on top) - but the semantic content collided and required manual reconciliation (t-2384 cancelled as superseded by t-2385). Worth considering as a related class of concurrent-session hazard when scoping the fix: even if write-path atomicity is solid, there's no mechanism to detect "another session already decided/closed this same task differently."
2026-07-24 RESOLUTION: Root cause is NOT a gap in brana's own write path. Verified: load_raw/save_tasks (brana-core/src/tasks.rs) already write via write_atomic (temp file in same dir + fs::rename, POSIX-atomic) under an exclusive lock_tasks/lock_tasks_timeout flock on a `.json.lock` sidecar, held across the full load-mutate-save cycle. Every CLI (backlog.rs) and MCP (backlog_add.rs/backlog_set.rs) write call site was checked — all route through this same lock+atomic-rename path, no direct fs::write to tasks.json bypasses it. Atomic rename guarantees a reader that already has the file open keeps reading the old inode to EOF; it cannot observe a torn/partial write from brana's own writers.
Likely actual source: an out-of-band writer that doesn't go through write_atomic at all — most plausibly git operations (checkout/merge) rewriting the working-tree tasks.json in place on a shared main checkout, which is exactly the class of hazard the worktree-only branching hard rule (t-2216/t-2206) exists to reduce, but git itself is outside brana's control so it can't be eliminated at the write-path level.
DECISION: implemented a bounded, low-risk read-side defense rather than a lock on reads (reads are deliberately unlocked for performance per backlog_get.rs's own comment) or chasing every possible external writer. load_tasks/load_raw now retry a JSON *parse* failure only (never an I/O error, e.g. file-not-found fails immediately) up to 3 times with a 15ms backoff, re-reading the file fresh each attempt via a new read_with_retry() helper. This self-heals a transient torn read once the racing external writer finishes, with no behavior change on the common non-racing path (retry only triggers on an actual parse failure). Commit 239803f8. Full workspace test suite green (1000+ tests). Doc entry: docs/architecture/features/backlog-v3-schema.md (t-2380 bullet).
Merged to dev — worktree cleaned up.
tasks.description:
`brana backlog get <id>` / `brana backlog query --json` can return invalid JSON (control-character parse error, confirmed via both jq and Python's json.loads) when another session is concurrently writing tasks.json for the same or a nearby task. Reproduced live 4+ times during t-2375's close session (2026-07-24): once while another session appended context to t-2325, and repeatedly during the epic-detection Tier 2a/2b live dogfood run at session close, where several in-progress tasks (t-2173, t-2214, t-2249) hit the same parse error.

Isolated single reads of the same task succeeded cleanly every time — the failure only appears under concurrent read/write load, consistent with a torn read (reader observes a partially-written file) rather than a deterministic data bug. `brana backlog set`/`add` are documented as atomic ("no need to read-modify-write"), but this suggests either the write path isn't fully atomic (no rename-based swap) or reads aren't taking any lock/snapshot against an in-flight write.

Impact so far: contained — callers that already degrade gracefully (e.g. t-2375's resolve_epic_ancestor(), which treats a jq/parse failure as "no epic found" and falls through the cascade) are unaffected in outcome, just silently lose a signal. But any caller that assumes `brana backlog get` always returns valid JSON (most call sites do) could crash or misbehave under concurrent sessions — which this repo demonstrably has right now (confirmed: a second live session was committing to dev on t-2322/t-2378 during this same close).

Investigate: (1) whether tasks.json writes use atomic write+rename or an in-place write, (2) whether reads should take a shared lock or read a consistent snapshot, (3) how many CLI/MCP read paths currently assume valid JSON without a parse-failure fallback.
tasks.notes: Root cause: brana's own write path already atomic+locked (write_atomic rename + lock_tasks flock, verified all CLI/MCP write call sites). Torn reads come from out-of-band writers outside brana's control (most likely git checkout/merge on a shared checkout). Fix: bounded parse-failure retry (3x, 15ms backoff) added to load_tasks/load_raw in brana-core/src/tasks.rs. Commit 239803f8. cargo test --workspace: all green. ./validate.sh: 0 errors, 233 pre-existing warnings (unrelated).
tasks.subject: Investigate tasks.json concurrent-write torn-read hazard

Implementation follow-up from t-2378's design decision (2026-07-24). Decided direction: adopt option b1 (build-fingerprint skew guard) as the structural fix, with faster ship-to-main cadence for schema-sealing changes as cheap insurance - not either alone.

Grounded findings from t-2378's design sketch (full report in that task's context):
- Current dev source is already fully sealed (set_field's whitelist, backlog_add's deny_unknown_fields) - both live incidents (t-2325/t-2377) came from a STALE COMPILED BINARY, not a source gap.
- Two independent staleness dimensions: (1) build-from-main lag (dev sealed, main not yet rebuilt), (2) running-process lag (MCP is a long-lived stdio process from ~/.local/bin/brana-mcp; even after reinstalling the binary, a live CC session keeps the OLD process until CC restarts).
- bootstrap.sh does neither build nor restart the MCP - only registers the binary path in .claude.json.
- Version stamp (CARGO_PKG_VERSION) is useless for skew detection - workspace version rarely bumps.

Implementation direction (decided: WARN, not hard-block - never lock out a legitimately-ahead dev session mid-work):
1. Stamp the binary at build time with git rev-parse HEAD (vergen/build.rs), exposed via a cheap mcp__brana__version tool or `brana --build-hash`.
2. Commit a schema-fingerprint file, bumped whenever set_field's whitelist or backlog_add's schema changes.

tasks.context:
Design sketch from t-2378 (2026-07-24):

Where the check lives: inside brana-core's write path (shared by both the `brana` CLI and `brana-mcp` binaries, since both link brana-core) — not in bootstrap.sh and not solely in validate.sh. This is what makes it binary-version-agnostic: whichever binary is running, old or new, enforces against the same rule.

What it checks against: rather than a version *number* (which only tells you "old" vs "new", not "which fields are retired"), embed the retired-field list directly as a compiled-in constant in brana-core (e.g. a RETIRED_FIELDS: &[&str] = &["level", "epic"] alongside the existing field whitelist). Any write path that serializes a field onto a task record checks it against RETIRED_FIELDS before persisting, in addition to (not instead of) the existing whitelist check that t-2310 already added. This makes the guard self-contained per-binary: an old binary that predates a sealing change won't have the new RETIRED_FIELDS entry (can't fix binaries that don't know a field is retired yet), but a binary that already ships the sealing logic can never regress even if invoked in a stale process/env, and there's no separate marker file to keep in sync or go stale itself.

What happens on mismatch: hard-refuse, not warn. This is a data-corruption bug (t-2325/t-2381 already happened 3x with a "warn after the fact" backstop — validate.sh check 63 — and still required 3 manual cleanups), so the write should return an error to the MCP/CLI caller rather than silently succeed-with-a-warning. Precedent: t-2310's set_field() whitelist already hard-rejects unknown fields; RETIRED_FIELDS is the same mechanism applied to fields that were once valid and are now sealed.

Residual gap this does NOT close: a binary built *before* a field was added to RETIRED_FIELDS still can't reject it — that binary literally doesn't know the field is retired yet. This guard only prevents *regression* once a binary has shipped the retired-field entry; it doesn't shrink the exposure window during the sealing work itself on dev, before that sealing commit reaches main. Nothing can, without either (a) not doing incremental schema-sealing work on dev while a live stale binary still points at the same shared tasks.json, or (b) fast-tracking schema-sealing commits specifically (see t-2378's process-fix recommendation, applied as a narrow exception to ADR-060's normal main-lags-dev buffer).

Scope note: keep this to the retired-field guard only. Do not build a general schema-version marker/skew-detection system (e.g. embedding a semver the binary checks against a source-of-truth file) — it adds a second thing to keep in sync (the marker itself) without preventing more than the simpler RETIRED_FIELDS constant does, since the actual failure mode we've seen is always "old binary still knows about a since-retired field," never "old binary doesn't understand a field format change it should ideally warn about."

tasks.notes:
DIAGNOSIS (investigation, 2026-07-24):

The recurring Read tool-fail on ~/.claude/agent-memory/brana-challenger/CALIBRATION.md (x48) is a prompt-ambiguity bug in system/agents/challenger.md, not a genuinely stale/moved file path.

Two distinct concepts exist and are correctly separated on disk, but NOT clearly disambiguated in the agent's own prompt text:
1. Static severity rubric: system/agents/CALIBRATION.md (5.1K, confirmed exists) -- linked via relative markdown links [CALIBRATION.md](CALIBRATION.md) at challenger.md:99 and :119. Since bootstrap.sh no longer file-copies agents (confirmed: bootstrap.sh:227-241 actively rm -rf's any stale ~/.claude/agents/ dir -- "Skills, commands, and agents are now provided by the plugin (system/)"), this relative link correctly resolves against the plugin's own system/agents/ directory when the agent runs from the repo checkout.
2. Dynamic per-run memory: challenger.md's frontmatter `memory: user` injects ~/.claude/agent-memory/brana-challenger/ (CC-native agent memory). That directory correctly uses the sharded MEMORY.md-index + calibration_*.md-per-topic pattern (confirmed: 150+ calibration_*.md files, zero monolithic CALIBRATION.md -- this is by design, matching this project's own auto-memory convention).

The bug: challenger.md's body text describes concept 2 ("your own agent memory directory... where you persist calibration notes") in the same breath as concept 1's CALIBRATION.md links, with no explicit statement of where each actually lives. This is exactly the ambiguity an LLM reasoning over its own prompt would conflate -- the agent attempts to read "CALIBRATION.md" from inside its memory directory (concept 2's location) instead of relative to its own definition file (concept 1's actual location), recurring fresh each time the agent runs (hence x48 across sessions, not a one-time stale reference).

None of the task's three original hypotheses is quite right: the read path isn't simply "wrong" (both real paths exist and are correct for what they hold), the file wasn't "moved/renamed" (both files are exactly where they should be), and the frontmatter memory migration didn't obsolete the read pattern (the memory:user migration is correct and unrelated to the static rubric file). The actual cause is prompt-level ambiguity between two correctly-placed but confusingly-juxtaposed concepts.

Recommended action (not implemented here -- diagnosis only, per task scope):
- Fix challenger.md: disambiguate the CALIBRATION.md references from the memory-directory description -- e.g. state explicitly "this file lives beside challenger.md in system/agents/, NOT in your memory directory" near both link occurrences, or restructure so the two concepts aren't adjacent in the prompt.

Feeds wave-1 superseding ADR (t-2397). No fix implemented in this task (investigation strategy, read-only).

RESET DONE. Entry q-11f6693ed40fcc3d now processed:false failed:false retry_count:0 error:null. AC met. Scoped to the ID deliberately — bare `reset-retries` would reset ALL failed-but-unprocessed entries.

ROOT CAUSE (task premise was WRONG). The task asserted schema-invalid meant a genuine contract mismatch. It did not. The Gemini CLI demanded re-authentication and printed an OAuth URL to stdout while exiting 0; the validator JSON-parsed that prose, failed, and the script buckets any parse failure as schema-invalid. Raw payloads, from ~/.claude/scheduler/logs/close-extraction/2026-06-29-074134.log and 2026-06-30-091708.log:
  attempt 1/3: raw[:300]='Authentication required. Please visit the URL to log in: https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/auth?...'
  attempt 2/3: raw[:300]='Error: timed out waiting for response'   (CLI blocking on the browser OAuth flow)
  attempt 3/3: identical auth prompt, different code_challenge
Environmental, and gone. Auth currently valid.

CONTRACT DRIFT RULED OUT (not merely inferred): system/cron/prompts/close-extraction.txt last changed e1fe2c3f 2026-06-12 (17 days BEFORE the failure); system/cron/close-extraction.sh last changed 1621b484 2026-06-19. Byte-identical to what ran on 2026-06-29. Validator at close-extraction.sh:236-269 requires parseable JSON with a learnings array; type in {errata,pattern,field-note}; size in {SMALL,LARGE}; non-empty title. agy is now 1.1.6 vs floor AGY_MIN_VERSION=1.0.10 — passes.

TRANSIENCE EVIDENCE: 60 entries processed since 2026-07-20, 44 with propagate:true (the same two-pass agy path this entry takes), 32 with commit_count>=10 (largest 143). 2026-07-23 log processed=21. This was the ONLY failed/stale entry in the queue.

PRECONDITIONS OK: snapshot /home/martineserios/.claude/sessions/snap-20260628-215311-547111.diff present (250.8K; exceeds MAX_DIFF_BYTES=100000 so only the first 100KB inlines — normal handled path, adds a truncation note). git_root .../clients/bemol/bemol-rails/.git exists and f5527c9 still reachable, so the L3 propagation pass gets real repo state. No staleness gate blocks reprocessing — close-extraction.sh:91 'stale' is a >3-day self-monitor/reminder counter, not a skip condition. Expect processing on the next nightly run; verify then.

DEADLINE THIS BEAT BY 5 DAYS: two 30-day reapers converge 2026-07-29 — (1) close-extraction.sh:487 `find ~/.claude/sessions -name 'snap-*.diff' -mtime +30 -delete` is STATUS-BLIND, and the snapshot mtime is 2026-06-28 21:53; (2) `brana close-queue prune` drops failed entries older than 30 days.

CORRECTION to this task's brief and to my own earlier note in this field: the quota category is `quota-exhausted:`, not `agy-empty-output:` (retired in t-2085, ADR-052). And the right fix for the miscategorisation is NOT 'route to agy-error' as I first wrote — it is to route auth-prompt/timeout output to skip_entry (the `quota-exhausted:` treatment), which preserves retry budget and breaks the loop, rather than fail_entry which burns a strike.

FOLLOW-UPS SPOTTED, NOT FILED (no user request):
1. close-extraction.sh:212 guard only greps `429|rate.?limit|resource_exhausted`. Adding 'Authentication required' and 'timed out waiting for response' would have made this entry self-heal the next night with zero human involvement.
2. DATA-LOSS RISK: the status-blind snapshot sweep destroys recoverable work — a failed entry still inside its retry window loses its snapshot at 30 days even though the queue entry survives, turning a retryable failure permanent. Worth gating on `processed || retry_count >= MAX_RETRIES`.
Both match pattern_error-categories-must-map-to-failure-surfaces_2026-06-12.

tasks.context:
CORRECTION (2026-07-24, caught by user mid-task): the original framing ("filter the whole brana:* namespace") was wrong. Namespace prefix isn't the right discriminator — several brana:*-namespaced skills are genuinely domain/project-specific and should keep being suggested exactly like a marketplace skill would: brana:meta-templates (WhatsApp BSP templates, per-client ~/.config/brana/meta/<client>.env), brana:gsheets, brana:mcp-builder, brana:rust-skills, brana:python-skills, etc. Filtering by namespace would wrongly suppress these.
The correct discriminator is: is this skill ALWAYS LOADED regardless of task context (the "6 Jobs" hot-path skills — build, backlog, close, do, docs, and similar universal skills listed in CLAUDE.md's command table) vs. a skill that's conditionally relevant (domain-specific, client-specific, or tech-specific)? Only the former category should be excluded from suggestion — suggesting "you might want /brana:build" is noise because it's already active every session; suggesting "you might want /brana:meta-templates" for a WhatsApp client task is exactly the useful signal the mechanism exists for.
Fix: build (or reuse, if one already exists) an explicit always-loaded/core skill list — not a namespace-prefix check — and filter the suggestion candidate pool against that list.

DATA-LOSS RISK found while resolving t-2442 (2026-07-24).

system/cron/close-extraction.sh:487 runs `find ~/.claude/sessions -name 'snap-*.diff' -mtime +30 -delete` with no reference to queue state. A close-queue entry that is still failed-but-retryable loses its snapshot at 30 days even though the queue entry itself survives — converting a recoverable failure into a permanent one, since the entry can then only ever fail `snapshot-missing`.

This nearly bit us: entry q-11f6693ed40fcc3d (bemol-rails, snapshot mtime 2026-06-28 21:53, 250.8K) would have had its snapshot deleted on the first nightly run after 2026-07-28. It was reset on 2026-07-24, 5 days inside the window. A second 30-day reaper (`brana close-queue prune`, line 482) drops failed entries older than 30 days, so the two converge on roughly the same date.

Fix: gate the snapshot sweep on queue state — only delete when the corresponding entry is `processed` OR has `retry_count >= MAX_RETRIES` (i.e. genuinely unrecoverable). Deleting the payload while the work item is still live is the wrong order of operations regardless of age.

Consider also whether prune and the snapshot sweep should share one definition of "dead", rather than two independent 30-day timers that happen to coincide.

AC: snapshots for processed or retries-exhausted entries are still reaped at 30 days (the sweep must not become a no-op leak)

tasks.context:
Found 2026-07-27 while listing the anita-envios backlog in proyecto_anita.

REPRO (proyecto_anita):
  brana backlog epics            -> 'anita-envios  90/109  82%'   (18 epics listed)
  brana backlog query --epic anita-envios --count -> 0
  jq '[.tasks[]|select(.epic=="anita-envios")]|length' .claude/tasks.json -> 109

ROOT CAUSE: the two commands use different definitions of 'epic'.
- 'backlog epics' reads the flat .epic STRING field on each task.
- 'query --epic' (added in t-2279) resolves the epic by walking .parent up to the nearest type:"epic" node and matching its .subject. It ignores the flat field entirely.
Per ADR-065 the ancestor-walk IS the intended model (cf. 'backlog add --epic', already a deprecated no-op with a stderr warning). The defect is the inconsistency plus the silent-empty failure, not the walk itself.

WHY IT BITES: proyecto_anita is unmigrated — 1068 tasks carry a flat .epic value but only ONE type:"epic" node exists (t-2220 agent-commercial-intelligence). So --epic returns 0 for every real epic, with no warning, while the epics dashboard right next to it reports healthy counts. An agent or human reading '0 tasks' concludes the epic is empty/done and moves on. Had to fall back to a jq union of (.epic field OR 'anita-envios' tag) to get the true 33 open tasks. Same class as the existing memory note 'backlog-v3-epic-ancestor-walk-finds-nothing-in-this-project' (that one is about /brana:backlog start branch naming; this is the query surface).

Also inconsistent: 'query --epic' silently accepts an unknown slug rather than erroring, so a typo and an unmigrated project are indistinguishable.

DIRECTION (pick one, do not do both silently):
(a) make 'query --epic' fall back to the flat .epic field when the ancestor walk finds no epic node, or
(b) keep the walk strict but WARN on stderr when 0 epic nodes match the slug AND N>0 tasks carry it as a flat value ('N tasks carry epic=X as a legacy flat field; this project has not been migrated to ADR-065 epic nodes'), and
(c) either way, make 'backlog epics' use the same resolution as 'query --epic' so the dashboard and the filter can never disagree.
Decide whether unmigrated projects get a migration path (flat field -> epic nodes) or permanent dual-read; ADR-065 should say which.

The premise was inverted: the wiring WAS present in system/scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit all along (the task checked .git/hooks/pre-commit, the stale installed copy). It was never REACHED.

Two stacked defects:
1. The hook resolved its message source as the literal .git/COMMIT_EDITMSG and exit 0'd when missing. In a linked worktree .git is a FILE, so it never resolves — and the early exit abandoned the ENTIRE hook. The attribution backstop, secret scan (t-2138), context-budget gate (t-2177) and red-verification (t-2216) were ALL skipped. Worktrees are mandatory per git-discipline.md, so every feature commit bypassed all four. This is much wider than the reported symptom.

2026-07-28 (thebrana, knowledge-pipeline lane) — THIRD live occurrence, plus one ADDITIVE facet this task did not previously cover.

THIRD OCCURRENCE. COMPLETED came back as t-1781,t-2398,t-2482,t-2488,t-2495,t-2496,t-2500,t-2501,t-2502,t-2503,t-2504,t-2505,t-2506,t-2507 — 14 IDs, of which the closing session owned 4. Of the 14 IDs above, t-2488 and t-2505 were `in_progress` at that moment, t-1781 was `in_progress` and deliberately left so by a --continue close, and t-2496 was `cancelled`. tasks.context:
Problem (user, 2026-07-27): the context assembled when addressing a task tends to over-fetch. Example given: context for sibling tasks under an epic that will not be worked on this session gets pulled in anyway. That is one instance of a general shape — components, designed behaviours, and patterns are not currently designed with awareness of what they cost in context.

Aim: assemble the exact context needed for the work at hand, with a reliable path to fetch more on demand, always aiming at the right context size. Perfect aim is unattainable and that is accepted; the point is that context sizing becomes an explicit design constraint that each component is designed against, rather than an afterthought.

Live evidence from the session where this was raised: SessionStart injected a 147-line memory index, a 58-item intelligence feed, and a 561-reminder count before the user had said anything.

Prior art in-repo to reconcile against, not duplicate: rules/context-budget.md (thresholds + expensive-operation guidance), rules/retrieval-routing.md / ADR-064 (pick the cheapest retrieval surface by query shape), the skill phase-file protocol (load procedure only when its subcommand is invoked). This task generalises those point solutions into a stated constraint plus an audit.

Adjacent narrower tasks (do not duplicate; likely children or dependencies): t-1368 audit CLAUDE.md hierarchy and context budget across nesting levels, t-1499 measure context budget consumed by /brana:close.

Scope note: L and cross-cutting. Per CLAUDE.md, M+ requires a feature spec in docs/architecture/features/ before writing to system/. Expected to decompose via /brana:backlog plan into per-surface children (session-start injection, skill LOAD steps, agent memory frontmatter, task/epic context assembly, retrieval).

Why this is P1 rather than cosmetic: _shared/epic-ancestor-walk.md's resolve_epic_ancestor() does `json=$(brana backlog get "$cur")` then `jq -r '.type'` / `jq -r '.parent'`. Wrong-epic routing is the documented t-2263 harm class: `brana session write` keys the handoff by epic and replaces rather than merges, so a mis-resolved slug clobbers another epic's state. The same walk is used by /brana:backlog start for branch naming.

Two fixes, both wanted: (1) serializer escapes control chars so output is always valid JSON; (2) resolve_epic_ancestor stops failing open — either use `brana backlog get --field <f>` (jq-free, verified working) or check jq's exit status and surface an error rather than returning empty.

tasks.context:
Raised by user 2026-07-27 after researching the July 2026 "loops are old, now graphs" trend.

THE TREND, WITH THE HYPE STRIPPED. Loop engineering named June 2026; graph engineering July 2026 (Steinberger 2026-07-18: "Are we still talking loops or did we shift to graphs yet?"). Framing that survives scrutiny: loops made individual agent BEHAVIOUR programmable, graphs make the ORGANISATION of agents programmable; and Ksenia Se's deflation — "a loop is already a graph, one whose path returns to an earlier node." The real shift is WHO routes: predictable routing in code, model reserved for interpretation/judgment. Prior art is decades old (state machines, DAGs, workflow engines; LangGraph shipped Jan 2024). DO NOT propagate the viral "graphs replaced RAG, 18% accuracy / 85% cost" claim — Turing Post traced it to one industrial-diagram case study, generalised falsely.

WHAT BRANA ALREADY HAS (the brainstorm must start here, not from a blank page). .claude/workflows/ holds three working graphs: sweep.js (fan-out finders -> cluster -> verify), verify-findings.js (N diverse-lens skeptics, majority vote), hive-mind.js (diverse workers -> adversarial verify -> synthesize). The Workflow tool's pipeline() vs parallel() distinction IS the graph-vs-barrier decision. Agents in system/agents/ are already nodes with isolated context and scoped tools; hooks are already deterministic edges.

WHAT V3 ALREADY SCOPES. t-2423 parallel candidate-prep on ephemeral worktrees (fan-out), t-2424 wire verify-findings as the cockpit judge stage (fan-in), t-2422 cockpit review-loop contract, t-2427 per-phase model/effort profiles, t-2429 loop tests, and critically t-2428 "retire manual phase invocations + prose routing rules" — which is literally "move routing out of prose and into code."

THE ACTUAL QUESTION, therefore, is NOT "should brana adopt graphs" (it already has them). It is: does the graph framing expose anything v3's design currently gets wrong or leaves implicit? Candidate angles worth stress-testing — where is routing still prose that should be code (delegation-routing.md itself is a prose routing table); are barriers used where pipelines would do (parallel() vs pipeline() misuse costs wall-clock); is there a missing typed contract between nodes; should skills-as-loops (t-2278) be skills-as-graphs; does the close/build phase-file protocol want explicit edges. Also in scope: the honest null result — "v3 is already right, this is vocabulary not architecture" is a valid and valuable verdict, and should be recorded as such rather than manufacturing changes.

ENTRY: /brana:brainstorm, then premortem before any ADR (pattern_brainstorm-premortem-before-adr), then /brana:challenge --deep on the resulting shape. Load-bearing outcome -> ADR in docs/architecture/decisions/.

2026-07-28 — CONCRETE AGENDA ITEM, from the t-2502 build that halted at DIAGNOSE. This task has been deferred three times for being abstract. It is no longer abstract: below is a three-times-reproduced defect that IS an instance of "does the graph framing expose anything v3's design currently gets wrong or leaves implicit — is there a missing typed contract between nodes."

THE FINDING: v3 has no LANE identity, and epic is being used as one.

ADR-065 defines epic as "what we're building, empty = feature done" — a DELIVERABLE. Session handoff state is keyed by epic. But a lane is an EXECUTION CONTEXT (which worktree, which branch, which session). Keying by epic uses a "what" as a "where", so two parallel sessions building toward one deliverable collide by construction. This is a category error in the choice of key, not a bug in the keying logic.

EVIDENCE (live, thebrana, 2026-07-28): all 24 session-state files return has_session_id false — the store carries no session identity whatsoever. Three files already claim epic "harness-core" (harness-core / async-close / thinking), filename slug and inner epic field drifted apart. The default session-state.json was written 16:55:03Z, after the close epic file at 16:02:23, so the global-max close anchor currently resolves to a different session's state. Symptoms traced to this one cause: t-2502 (close window anchors on another lane's timestamp — 3 reproductions, worst case a ZERO-commit window that Step 1 misreads as read-only and skips the snapshot entirely, losing a whole session to the nightly async extraction), t-2506 (same-day second close cannot update its own next[]), and the operator-reported sitrep ambiguity (opening a new session, cannot tell whether the handoff is this lane's or a parallel lane's).

WHAT V3 GIVES vs WHAT A LANE NEEDS — audited:
- epic node (status/wip_limit/gate/contract/auto-close): identifies a deliverable. NOT a lane.
- key:value tags (schema D8, queryable — the mechanism ADR-065 used to dissolve the initiative node): could carry a lane/session key with NO new node level. Strong candidate.
- task.branch: already written by `backlog start`; already 1:1 with a worktree by git-discipline's worktree HARD RULE; `backlog start` already claims by branch (claims_claim claimant "agent:{branch}:session"). The lane identity ALREADY EXISTS in the backlog — the session store just does not reference it.
- waves ({selector, contract, gate, status}): the closest thing v3 has to a process/lane object, and `backlog_wave_list` returns [] — BUILT AND ENTIRELY UNUSED. A second finding of the same kind: v3 shipped a process primitive and nothing routes through it. Worth a verdict of its own.

CONSTRAINT for any design: the lane key must be captured at session START, not read at close — 15 of 24 state files record branch "dev" because closes happen after merge, so branch collapses at close time.

SEPARATE, DO NOT CONFLATE: a contiguous git range A..B cannot express a non-contiguous commit set. Even a perfect lane-scoped anchor leaves a concurrent lane's interleaved commits inside the range (measured: 11-commit window holding 2 own commits). Eliminating that needs per-commit recording plus a --commits LIST interface into close-snapshot.sh, which today accepts only --git-range. Decide explicitly whether this is in or out of the ADR.

The operator's framing, which is the right one: "this needs to be orchestrated with backlog — we work on tasks defined on backlog, we need a structure that helps."

Blocks t-2490 (explicit scope challenge to t-2278's audit-backed plan).



2026-07-28 — EVIDENCE for the two open questions in the agenda note above, measured live by a parallel session (96f57378) that had started t-2502 before reading the halt. Contributed as evidence, NOT as a verdict; the ADR decision remains this task's.

Q1: "the lane key must be captured at session START, not read at close." A capture point already exists and is unused.
- system/hooks/session-start.sh is a real SessionStart hook that already computes SESSION_ID (from stdin JSON .session_id), CWD, and GIT_ROOT, and already writes BRANA_PROJECT / BRANA_SESSION_ID / BRANA_EFFORT_LEVEL into $CLAUDE_ENV_FILE. Adding a lane pin there costs one file write at a point that already has every field a lane key needs.
- BUT: BRANA_SESSION_ID is SET AND NOT EXPORTED. Verified: `export -p | grep -c BRANA_SESSION_ID` = 0, and `bash -c 'echo $BRANA_SESSION_ID'` prints UNSET. So the session id is visible to the model's own shell and to NOTHING it spawns. Any lane design that expects a child process, a git hook, or a delegated script to read the session id from the environment will silently get an empty key. This is a hard constraint on the mechanism, not a detail.

Q2: "Decide explicitly whether per-commit recording is in or out of the ADR." Three findings that change its cost:
- git REFLOG already distinguishes created-here from arrived-here, with no committer-date heuristic. Reason strings measured: `commit:` / `commit (initial):` / `commit (merge):` for commits CREATED in this working tree, vs `merge X: Fast-forward`, `checkout: moving from A to B`, `reset: moving to HEAD` for history that merely arrived. This is the exact predicate a per-commit ledger needs, and git maintains it already.
- LINKED WORKTREES HAVE THEIR OWN HEAD REFLOG (probed). So per-worktree lane isolation is FREE and RETROACTIVE — it works for sessions that started before any new mechanism ships, and a concurrent lane in its own worktree is excluded by construction. This makes "which commits are mine" answerable today for the worktree-per-lane case, which git-discipline already mandates. The residual gap is only two sessions sharing ONE checkout (e.g. both on dev in the main tree) — which is exactly the case the three t-2502 reproductions came from.
- post-commit git hooks DO fire in linked worktrees (probed; both a main-tree and a worktree commit fired it). The pattern_worktree-git-is-a-file-hooks-inert note is about hard-coded .git/<path> resolution, NOT about hooks failing to fire. So a post-commit capture point is viable; its blocker is Q1's attribution problem (no exported session id), not worktree mechanics.

Implication worth a line in the ADR: reflog gives lane identity for worktree-separated lanes for free, so per-commit recording may only be needed to cover shared-checkout lanes. If the ADR instead makes worktree-per-lane a hard invariant, the per-commit ledger may be unnecessary entirely.

tasks.context:
Raised by user 2026-07-27, immediately after the graph-engineering research (see t-2488).

THE PROPOSAL. Skills today are large procedures (build, close, backlog each carry multi-step phase files). The proposal: make skills ATOMIC — small units with one job, a typed input and a typed output — and achieve complex procedures by composing those atoms in loops and graphs. The same atom is then reusable across different graphs instead of being locked inside one skill's procedure. Explicitly framed by the user as "we need to design to do graph engineering."

TENSION WITH t-2278 — DO NOT PAPER OVER THIS. t-2278 (skills-as-loops) was right-sized by a REAL AUDIT to a focused L refactor and deliberately scoped this out: "22 skills stay skills (untouched — churn de-risked)", "NOT 35-skill rewrite", and the "pipeline/assembly-line model = deferred north-star/final wave, out of initial scope". This task is close to that parked north-star and reopens the churn t-2278 chose to avoid. That earlier caution was evidence-based, so this design must either (a) show why the audit's conclusion no longer holds, or (b) find a decomposition that gets graph-composability WITHOUT the 35-skill rewrite. "The audit was too conservative" is a claim requiring evidence, not an assumption. Per user decision 2026-07-27: this is a SEPARATE task from t-2278, gated on t-2488 — t-2278's de-risked plan stays intact unless this design earns the reopening.

CARRY FORWARD FROM t-2278 (already decided, do not relitigate): default to CODE-AS-ORCHESTRATOR — deterministic control flow via Workflow scripts + wave-drain — NOT an LLM supervisor. Anthropic's orchestrator-workers pattern is reserved only for open-ended tasks whose subtasks cannot be predetermined. Conveyor = code; stations = specialized worker agents; advance/bounce routing = verifier VERDICTS feeding deterministic routing. An orchestrator agent earns a station only where "good enough to advance?" is irreducible judgment, and even then it is modelled as a verifier returning a verdict, not a pipeline-wide supervisor.

DESIGN QUESTIONS THIS MUST ANSWER. What is the atom — a phase file? a single tool-scoped agent? something smaller? What is the contract between atoms (typed schema in/out, like the Workflow tool's schema option)? How does an atom stay independently invocable by a human while also being graph-callable? What carries state across atoms without re-injecting whole context (ties directly to t-2484 context economy — atomicity is a context-economy lever, since a small atom loads only what it needs). Which existing skills are genuinely composite vs genuinely atomic — start from an audit, not a blank page. How do the existing graphs (sweep.js, verify-findings.js, hive-mind.js) already demonstrate the atom/graph split, and what is missing to generalise them.

WATCH FOR: over-decomposition. Atoms too small produce graph plumbing that costs more than the monolith it replaced, and every hop is a context re-entry. The design should state the granularity floor and justify it.

tasks.context:
Hit live 2026-07-27, thebrana, on a second /brana:close --continue in the same session.

MECHANISM. gate-and-evidence.md Step 1 sets the session window with: LAST_CLOSE=$(brana session read --json | jq -r '.written_at'). But `brana session read` with no flags reads only the DEFAULT session-state.json. When the previous close set an epic (Step 9c), `brana session write` routes the handoff to the epic-keyed file instead — here session-state-brana-v3-redesign.json, written_at 2026-07-28T00:25:50Z. The default file still held 2026-07-27T21:57:01Z, so LAST_CLOSE came back ~2.5h stale.

BLAST RADIUS. COMMIT_COUNT computed as 32 instead of the 4 commits actually new since the prior close. That count drives (a) the Step 1b snapshot range, which would have re-queued ~28 commits already queued by the earlier close under a different range — the dedup in close-snapshot.sh keys on the range string, so a DIFFERENT range is not deduped and the same work gets extracted twice; (b) CHANGED_FILES, which drove the weight classification off a 36-file diff instead of the real 1-file diff; (c) Step 9c's COMPLETED accumulator list. Worked around this session by scoping the range by hand to 6d206522..HEAD.

Note the perverse incentive: the more faithfully a close follows Step 9c (set the epic so the handoff lands in its unit bucket, ADR-060/t-2154), the more certainly it breaks the NEXT close's anchor. Every epic-routed close poisons the following one.

FIX OPTIONS. `brana session read --all` already exists and surfaces epic-scoped files (last 30 days) — the gate could take the max written_at across all session files rather than the default file alone. Alternatively `brana session read` gains an --epic flag, or the default file gets a pointer/mtime touch on every epic-routed write. Prefer the read-side fix: writers are already correct per ADR-060, the reader is the one making a false assumption.

Adjacent, do not merge: t-2480 (epic accumulator COMPLETED over-reach on shared main) is a different symptom of over-broad windows; this task is the upstream cause for the epic-routed case.

AC: close Step 1 resolves LAST_CLOSE from the newest session state across default AND epic-keyed files
AC: a close following an epic-routed close computes a window containing only commits since that close, verified with a two-close-in-one-session repro
AC: fix documented in gate-and-evidence.md Step 1 so the anchor logic is not re-derived wrongly later

Hit 2026-07-27 starting t-2487 / t-2478 / t-2491 — all three are kind:fix with work_type:implement.

THE CONFLICT.
- ~/.claude/rules/task-convention.md: "Branch: feature=feat/, fix=fix/, refactor=refactor/, docs=docs/, research=research/, ops=chore/" — keyed on KIND.
- system/skills/backlog/phases/start.md "Branch creation" step 2: maps task.work_type -> prefix, where `implement`/`feat` -> `feat`. Keyed on WORK_TYPE, and has no `fix` input at all unless work_type is literally "fix".

So a bugfix task carrying work_type:implement resolves to `feat/` under start.md and `fix/` under task-convention.md. Resolved by hand this session in favour of `fix/` (user decision) — branches cut were cli-backlog-schema/fix/t-2487-*, close/fix/t-2478-*, close/fix/t-2491-*.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND COSMETICS. The prefix is the only signal in the branch name distinguishing a bugfix from a feature, and CLAUDE.md's branch convention lists `fix` as a first-class work-type. Labelling three P1/P2 defect branches `feat/` misreports the change class to anything reading branch names (validate checks, close classification, review routing).

LIKELY FIX. start.md's mapping should consult `kind` first and fall back to `work_type`, since `work_type:implement` is a cognitive-mode label ("this is coding work") and is deliberately orthogonal to what the change DOES — note task-convention.md already says "kind: refactor tasks use work_type: implement", confirming work_type is not meant to carry change class. Confirm which file is authoritative before editing; do not fix both independently or they will drift again.

- cmd_get serializes with serde_json::to_string_pretty / to_string, which escape U+0000-U+001F BY CONSTRUCTION. serde_json cannot emit the reported output. Equally, if tasks.json itself held a raw control char, serde_json would reject it at LOAD and the command would exit non-zero with empty stdout — not emit unparseable JSON.

2026-07-28 — ROOT-CAUSED, PARTIALLY REPRODUCED. Trigger is a TORN READ during a concurrent write, not a serializer defect.

WHAT HAPPENED (accidental, live). `brana backlog query --json | jq` had succeeded four times in a row earlier in the same session. It then failed with: "jq: parse error: Invalid string: control characters from U+0000 through U+001F must be escaped at line 19, column 102". Re-running the identical command ~60s later parsed cleanly, and a python scan for raw control chars over that later output found none. This session wrote nothing to tasks.json in the interval; the failing window coincides with a concurrent session writing it (worktree list changed across the same period: t-2496 removed, t-2492 appeared, main checkout advanced 35befb8a -> 4ce9b508).

AC HONESTY — the "capture the raw bytes before anything is changed" AC is NOT met. The failing output was already gone when the failure was noticed; what exists is the jq error string (with exact line/column) and a negative rescan, not the raw bytes. Anyone picking this up should still try to capture bytes under a deliberate race (see repro recipe below) rather than treat this note as closing that AC.

WHY THE EARLIER SWEEP FOUND NOTHING, AND WAS RIGHT. The t-2487 session concluded serde_json escapes control chars by construction and swept all 2138 task IDs finding zero parse errors, so AC1 was split here as unreproducible. That conclusion is CORRECT and is not contradicted: the file AT REST is always valid. The corruption exists only in a read that races a write — a reader observing a partially-written file. After-the-fact inspection cannot reproduce it by construction, which is exactly why it looked like a phantom.

DELIBERATE REPRO RECIPE (untried — for whoever takes this): loop `brana backlog query --json > /tmp/out.$$.json` in one shell while another loops `brana backlog set <some-task> notes "$(date)"`, and keep every output whose parse fails. That preserves the raw bytes the AC asks for.

IMPLICATION. Not a JSON/serialization bug; do not fix it in the serializer. It is the multi-writer/unsynchronized-reader gap on tasks.json. Same disease as the field note on epic auto-detection failing to converge under concurrency, which independently hypothesized "likely wants the same treatment as other multi-writer state (a lock, or collapsing to a single source of truth), not a retry/backoff patch". See pattern_file-lock-scope-classify-writers_2026-06-20 for the writer-classification approach. An atomic write (write-temp + rename) on the writer side may be the whole fix, since rename is atomic and readers would then always see one complete version.

SEVERITY. P3 was set when the trigger was unknown and the blast radius looked closed (jq is out of the epic-walk path). This affects every reader that pipes `backlog query --json` to jq while any other session writes — several skill procedures do exactly that. It fails LOUDLY (hard parse error, not silent bad data), which argues against P1. Recommend P2, routed with the concurrency cluster (t-2502 / t-2506 / sitrep ambiguity / epic-detection non-convergence) rather than fixed standalone — one write-discipline change closes all five.

CORRECTION, same session, ~20 minutes after the note above: the TORN READ root cause is REFUTED for brana's own write path and must not be treated as established.

brana-core/src/tasks.rs:918 save_tasks() calls write_atomic() (tasks.rs:832) — temp file in the SAME directory (same filesystem, so POSIX atomic replace holds), PID-scoped temp name, then std::fs::rename. On top of that, lock_tasks() takes an exclusive advisory flock(2) on a <store>.json.lock sidecar held across the ENTIRE read-modify-write (t-2166). So brana writers are both atomic AND serialized: a reader sees either the complete old inode or the complete new one, never a partial file. The observed parse failure cannot be explained by a brana write.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE: the failure was real, transient, and bracketed by successful runs of the identical command with no write from this session in between. WHAT IS NO LONGER CLAIMED: that a concurrent brana write caused it.

SURVIVING SUSPECTS, in rough order: (1) non-Rust writers that bypass both the lock and write_atomic — system/scripts/close-classify.sh and system/scripts/migrate/*.py (null-to-p3, remap-streams, normalize-tags, assign-initiatives-thebrana, extract-personal, collapse-level-epic-v3, drop-deprecated-fields) all touch tasks.json directly; whether any ran in the window is UNVERIFIED. (2) something in the shell/pipe layer rather than the file at all. (3) a reader path that does not go through load_raw.

NEXT STEP for whoever picks this up: audit the non-Rust writers for lock+atomic discipline FIRST (that is a real defect regardless of whether it caused this), and only then attempt the deliberate race repro described above. Do not fix anything in the serializer or in save_tasks — both are already correct.

P2 (raised in the note above) still stands on blast radius — every procedure that pipes backlog query --json to jq is exposed to a hard parse error — but the mechanism is OPEN, not solved.

tasks.context:
Found live 2026-07-27, in the very first close to run the t-2491 fix — caught by comparing the computed window against the actual commit list before trusting it.

OBSERVED. LAST_CLOSE resolved to 2026-07-28T01:29:49Z, written by a CONCURRENT session (which was working t-2496 in its own worktree and closed mid-flight). COMMIT_COUNT came back 4, and the window contained 3 commits from 22:29 onward. The closing session's actual work spanned 22:01 -> 22:51 (10 commits). Everything from 22:01-22:27 — including the t-2487/t-2478/t-2491/t-2493 fixes themselves — fell OUTSIDE the window and would not have been snapshotted or queued for extraction.

THE TRADE. Before t-2491 the anchor read only the default session-state.json, so an epic-routed close left it stale and the window OVER-reached (32 commits vs 4). After t-2491 it takes the max across all files, so a concurrent session's close makes the window UNDER-reach. Over-reach causes double-extraction (close-snapshot.sh dedups on the range string, so a different range is not deduped). Under-reach causes SILENT LOSS — the work is simply never queued, and nothing surfaces that it was skipped. Under-reach is the worse failure because it is invisible.

ROOT CAUSE. "Newest close anywhere" is the wrong question. The anchor wants "when did THIS session last close", which is a per-session/per-branch/per-epic quantity, not a global max. The global max is only correct when closes are strictly sequential — the assumption that concurrency breaks.

CANDIDATE FIXES (not yet chosen — needs the concurrency model decided first):
- Anchor on the newest close whose state matches THIS session's epic/branch, falling back to the global max only when no such entry exists.
- Key session state by session id as well as epic, and anchor on this session's own last close.
- Take the max but clamp it to no later than the first commit authored by this session/branch in the current window, so another session's close can never truncate.
- Emit a warning when the resolved anchor is NEWER than the oldest commit that would otherwise be in scope — at minimum make the truncation visible instead of silent.

Worked around for the 2026-07-27 close by passing an explicit --git-range 1a99cb45..HEAD.

Adjacent: t-2480 (epic accumulator over-reach on shared main) and t-2491 (the fix that introduced this). Do not revert t-2491 — the stale-default bug it fixed is real; this needs a better anchor, not the old one.
