2026-07-29 — CORRECTION AT START. THREE OF THIS TASK'S CLAIMS ARE WRONG. Do not work the ACs above as written; the corrected defect and ACs are below.

WRONG 1 — "the spec's fail-loud assert was never implemented". It IS implemented: assert_active_epic_resolves() at brana-core/src/tasks.rs:236, tests at tasks.rs:2963+, wired into brana-mcp/src/tools/backlog_focus.rs:43. The filing concluded "nothing asserts" from grepping the WIP-cap path only (check_epic_wip_cap), but the assert lives on the FOCUS path. Grepping one call site and generalising to "never implemented" is the error.

WRONG 2 — "decide whether active_epic stores an ID or a slug". Already decided: SLUG. ADR-066-active-epic-project-scoped-only.md (Accepted 2026-07-22), `brana backlog set-active <slug>` (t-2155), and assert_active_epic_resolves matching on an epic node's `subject`. There is no open fork here.

WRONG 3 — "the pointer holds a slug naming harness-core, which is status:next not active". The resolver STRIPS project-scoped keys when falling back to global (PROJECT_SCOPED_CONFIG_KEYS, util.rs:176, t-2158). So active_epic does not resolve to harness-core — it resolves to ABSENT. The filing read the raw global file with jq and bypassed the resolver it was supposed to be testing.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, MEASURED 2026-07-29 ON dev:
  .claude/tasks-config.json              ABSENT          <- ADR-066's sole authoritative source
  system/state/tasks-config.json         harness-core     <- thebrana's TRACKED deploy source
  ~/.claude/tasks-config.json            harness-core     <- global cache, written by sync-state.sh
  `brana backlog focus --top 2` -> t-2074, t-1073. Neither is under t-2345 (harness-core).
  Exit 0. No warning. No epic marker. Focus ran completely unscoped.

THE REAL DEFECT, AND IT IS NARROWER AND MORE INTERESTING THAN FILED:
thebrana is the repo that PRODUCES the global config (system/state/tasks-config.json -> sync-state.sh -> ~/.claude/tasks-config.json) while ADR-066 forbids ANY repo from READING that global file. thebrana therefore publishes the machine-wide active_epic and receives none itself. It is the only project structurally guaranteed to hit this, because it is the only one that owns the deploy source.

THE GUARD GAP, STATED PRECISELY: assert_active_epic_resolves fires only when active_epic is Some. thebrana's state is None. So the fail-loud path covers "set but unresolvable" and does NOT cover "absent" — and absent is the state that actually occurs here. backlog focus degrades to unscoped ranking with exit 0 and no signal, which is the silent-clean class (cf. t-2536, t-2546): a result that is indistinguishable from a correctly-scoped one.

THE ONE GENUINE OPEN QUESTION (was not in the original filing): what is the relationship between a new project-local .claude/tasks-config.json and the existing tracked system/state/tasks-config.json? THIS TASK FOLDS IN ADR-065 D4's PROMOTION REVIEW, which was due 2026-07-28 and passed unactioned. t-2535's closing notes state plainly: "the cap remains ADVISORY — D4's warn-vs-hard-block promotion review (due 2026-07-28) is untouched and still open". Filed as one task deliberately: "warn or block" and "which epics does it even apply to" are the same question about what the cap is, and splitting them would repeat the pattern this audit is about.

DEFECT 1 — WRONG SCOPE. backlog-v3-schema.md:65 says the cap is "only meaningful on the active epic". check_epic_wip_cap(all, parent_id) at tasks.rs:205 counts children of WHATEVER epic is being added to and never reads active_epic. So it fires on all 50 buckets rather than the one being worked. Every add to any epic warns. That is not a limit; it is a constant.

DEFECT 2 — THE UNITS ARE BUCKETS, NOT DELIVERABLES. The 50 t-23xx epics were bulk-created in one pass on 2026-07-23 (all P3, all wip_limit unset, no context) from the previously-flat `epic:` tag strings — harness-core, docs, session, research-inbox. A category bucket has no natural empty state, so no amount of closing or parking makes it go quiet. t-2535's context already reached this ("long-lived CATEGORY BUCKETS, so no amount of parking or draining can make them go quiet under the open-children metric") and it remains the operative fact.

MEASURED 2026-07-29: t-2359 74 open, t-2370 50, t-2338 48, t-2345 39, t-2348 32. Against a cap of 10. Meanwhile only 7-10 tasks are in_progress portfolio-wide and 0 of 601 pending tasks have `started` or `branch` set — so actual work-in-flight is nowhere near any cap.

WHY t-2535 DID NOT RESOLVE THIS, AND WHAT THAT COSTS. t-2535 was filed as "a warning with no consequence — enforce or retire", and completed the same day by making the cap honor parking. Its own notes record the outcome: "zero tasks are currently parked, so all three epics measured identically before and after" and "the cap remains ADVISORY". The warning got more accurate and stayed consequence-free. t-2531's framing (folded into t-2535) is the argument that still stands: a cap that warns on every add and blocks nothing TRAINS THE OPERATOR AND EVERY AGENT TO IGNORE WARNINGS FROM THIS TOOL, degrading the signal value of every other warning brana emits. Same class as ADR-069's fail-open and t-2536's silent-clean reconcile.

EVIDENCE THE TRAINING EFFECT IS REAL AND ONGOING: filing the four audit tasks on 2026-07-29 produced the cap warning four times and proceeded four times, as did the two filings before them. Six consecutive breaches in one session, dutifully reported, zero behavior change. That is the failure mode reproducing while being documented — the same thing t-2535's author described doing.

ADMISSIBLE OUTCOMES (pick one; "leave advisory" is what produced this state and is not on the list):
1. SCOPE + ENFORCE — cap applies only to the resolved active epic, and blocks over cap with a documented override. Requires t-2558 first. Real teeth, narrow blast radius.
2. RETIRE — drop cap and warning entirely. Honest about buckets being buckets; loses the signal. Note the audit found the cap is not measuring anything actionable today.
3. REDEFINE THE UNIT — keep a cap but apply it to something that can actually be empty (a wave per ADR-065, or in_progress). Note t-2535 already rejected plain in_progress-rescoping on the grounds that it would satisfy the AC by going silent rather than by gaining consequence — read that reasoning before re-proposing it.

Observed live 2026-07-29 closing proyecto_anita epic 'agent' (concurrent session active on the same epic file).

Three separate `brana session write` calls, each carrying 3 then 2 then 11 next[] entries, all returned bare {"ok":true,"path":...} and each time exactly the same 2 entries were absent from the written file. No stderr warning, no next{} stats block (the phase doc documents a response shape with incoming/written/dropped_duplicates/mode — this binary emits neither).

Ruled out:
- Not the case-folded-text dedup: all texts unique.
- Not a cap: agent-epic history shows a state with 40 next[] entries.
- Not CAS/base_written_at: attempt 3 passed a matching base_written_at read from the same epic key and still landed 9 of 11.

Second, separable finding in the same session: the 2nd write REPLACED rather than unioned (next 9->1, accomplished 15->0, learnings 13->0, blockers->0), destroying a concurrent session's freshly-written state. It was recovered only because that session happened to write again a minute later and session-history.jsonl had the pre-clobber row. So the union/replace behaviour is ALSO non-deterministic under concurrency, not just the drop.

Relates to t-2549 (base_written_at ignored, incumbent-wins dedup) — same surface, but that ticket describes entries SURVIVING when they should be replaced; this is entries VANISHING when they should be added. Likely the same merge routine.

Filed 2026-07-29 from a backlog-flow audit. This is the root finding; t-2558/t-2561 (WIP cap) and t-2560 (old cohort) are downstream of it. Design/decision task — do not start by writing code.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT MOTIVATES IT (2026-07-29, dev, 2431 tasks):

Completion latency, on the 711 completed tasks carrying both dates:
  same day  490 (69%)   <=1d 555 (78%)   <=7d 627 (88%)   >30d 33 (4.6%)   >90d 0 (ZERO)
Age of the 601 pending:
  <7d 94 (16%)   7-30d 30 (5%)   30-90d 267 (44%)   >90d 210 (35%)   oldest 148d

Zero completions have ever taken more than 90 days, while 210 pending tasks are older than 90 days. Those two facts together mean old tasks are not being worked slowly — they are not in the working set at all. Corroborated independently at monthly resolution (completions in month M are almost entirely tasks created in month M: Mar 298 created/267 completed, Apr 135/126, May 79/98, Jun 107/125, Jul 83/86).

HONEST LIMIT ON THE ABOVE: 715 of 1426 completions carry NO completed date, so latency is measured on the 711 that have one. I could not rule out that the undated half contains old-task closures. The monthly-cohort check draws on the same dated subset, so it corroborates but does not independently confirm. ANYONE TAKING THIS TASK SHOULD FIRST ESTABLISH WHY HALF THE COMPLETION RECORD IS UNDATED — it is both a data-quality defect in its own right and the main threat to this task's premise.

THE DIAGNOSIS. "Pending" conflates three populations with different physics:
  1. WORK IN FLIGHT — 7-10 in_progress portfolio-wide. Small and healthy. This is the only actual queue.
  2. A MID-SESSION CAPTURE BUFFER — findings filed while doing something else. Bursty: 49 tasks on 2026-07-24, 23 on 07-28, 14 on 07-27; 206 of the month's 260 creations landed in the final week. This is a LOG. A log growing is not a failure.
  3. A READING LIST — t-2359 research-inbox alone holds 69 of the 210 oldest tasks.
Corroboration that (2) and (3) were never work-in-flight: 0 of 601 pending tasks have `started` or `branch` set. Not one.

The v3 schema doc reached the same three-pile conclusion by inspection (backlog-v3-schema.md:28, "563 pending tasks that are really three unrelated piles (mechanical, judgment, a reading list)") but explicitly flagged it as "an interpretive read of their content, not a field-backed count". The measurements above are the field-backed version, and they agree.

WHY IT MATTERS. Every aggregate we compute spans all three. `brana backlog burndown` reports -160/month "growing", which reads as an emergency and is mostly capture inflow. The WIP cap counts buckets that mix all three. `backlog stale` (14-day default) would flag 477 tasks. None of these numbers can be acted on, so none of them are — which is the same trained-to-ignore dynamic as the cap warning (see t-2561).

QUESTIONS TO SETTLE (this is the decision, not the implementation):
1. Is the distinction a new field, a reuse of an existing one (tags:['parked'] already yields synthetic status 'parked' via classify() at tasks.rs:118-127 and is currently used by ZERO tasks), or a status value? Prefer reuse — t-1345 deliberately removed synthetic values from the raw status vocabulary and adding them back reverses that.
2. Does capture-class work appear in burndown/stale/WIP at all, or is it excluded from flow metrics by construction?
3. What promotes an item from capture to queue, and who does it? Without a promotion step, splitting the populations just relabels the pile.
4. Should `brana backlog burndown` report per-population rather than one net number?

AC: the population distinction is decided and recorded, with the reuse-vs-new-field question answered explicitly
AC: whatever mechanism is chosen, a promotion path from capture to queue exists and is documented — relabelling without it is not a fix
AC: flow metrics (burndown, stale, WIP) state which population they cover; no aggregate silently spans all three
AC: the undated-completion defect (715 of 1426) is either fixed or filed separately with its cause identified
AC: re-measured after the change — the reported numbers are ones a reader can act on

tasks.description:

  ~/.claude/projects/-home-martineserios-.claude-projects--home-martineserios-enter-thebrana-ventures-proyecto-anita-memory/memory/session-state-agent.json

A brand-new project bucket, slugged from the memory directory's own path. The real handoff file was untouched, so the close believed it had written state that no future session would ever read.

Proposed: resolve the bucket from the git repo identity (toplevel of the containing repo, or the common-dir for a worktree) rather than raw CWD; refuse and exit non-zero when CWD is not inside any git repo, or when the resolved slug does not match an existing project bucket unless an explicit --project/--force is passed. Anything is better than ok:true on a write nobody will read.

Separate from t-2562 (next[] entries silently dropped) — same command, different failure: that one loses entries within a correct file, this one writes a correct file in the wrong place.

DEFECT 1 — NO DERIVATION. system/skills/build/phases/close.md:227 reads:
  question: "dev is ahead of main by {N} commits. Ship dev->main and deploy?"
{N} is a bare placeholder. A grep for `rev-list --count` across system/ returns worktree-reaping logic and runner tests and NO deploy-gap derivation at all. A draft rule keyed on "system/ changed" was killed by pre-mortem — nearly every commit touches system/, so it would fire on almost every merge and become ignorable noise, the WIP-cap failure mode (t-2565).

2026-07-31 SUPERSEDED IN PART BY ADR-075 — READ THIS BEFORE IMPLEMENTING. Two lanes worked t-2547 concurrently on the same day; the other lane wrote docs/architecture/decisions/ADR-075-ship-on-deploy-surface-change.md (Accepted, commit 579f12c5). Where this task's ACs and ADR-075 disagree, THE ADR WINS.

WHAT THE ADR CHANGES:
1. THE METRIC. This task's AC says derive with `git rev-list --count main..dev`. ADR-075 rejects counting commits at all — the historical written-down numbers (12, 1, 10, 16, 55, 68) were untrustworthy BECAUSE they counted commits, which the ADR measured to be uncorrelated with deploy risk. The correct signal counts the DEPLOY SURFACE:
     git diff --name-only main..dev -- system/hooks system/rules system/agents system/cli | wc -l
   paired with a binary-staleness check (live ~/.local/bin/brana mtime vs newest system/cli commit). On 2026-07-31 that reads "13 deploy-relevant files, binary 4 days stale" instead of "68 commits".
2. THE TRIGGER. ADR-075 decides ship is EVENT-triggered on deploy-surface change: any commit touching system/hooks, system/rules, system/agents or system/cli is promoted and deployed on merge to dev; everything else rides along free (--ff-only admits no partial promotion, so the marginal risk is zero once a surface change justifies promotion).

WHY MY PRE-MORTEM WAS WRONG TO REJECT THAT TRIGGER: I killed an event-trigger on the grounds that "nearly every commit touches system/, so it would over-fire and become ignorable noise." I never measured it. ADR-075 did: of 48 changed files in the 68-commit batch, system/hooks 3, system/rules 0, system/agents 0, system/skills 3 — six deploy-relevant files plus a binary rebuild. Deploy-surface changes are RARE. The over-trigger objection is empirically false and the rest of that pre-mortem reasoning should not be leaned on either.

WHAT SURVIVES FROM THIS TASK: the located defect is still real and still unfixed — system/skills/build/phases/close.md:227 is a bare {N} placeholder with NO derivation anywhere in system/. Implement the derivation using ADR-075's deploy-surface query, NOT a commit count. The "wrong host" point (only build's CLOSE has the offer; /brana:close has none) also stands, though its causal story was refuted separately (see below).

REVISED ACs — the earlier AC block above is superseded:
AC: the deploy-pending signal is derived at read time from the DEPLOY SURFACE per ADR-075, never a commit count and never a written-down number
AC: a binary-staleness check accompanies it (live brana mtime vs newest system/cli commit)
AC: the offer is skipped when the deploy surface is unchanged
AC: /brana:close performs the same derived check, so a session ending without a build still sees it
AC: no time-based or size-based trigger is added (ADR-075 disqualifies both)
AC: grep for a hardcoded ahead-of-main count in system/ returns nothing

2026-07-31 NEW EVIDENCE (from t-2557's timeout-diagnostic fix, now merged): the killed child is drained before bailing, and the answer is:

  t-1336 FAILED — claude CLI (MCP) timed out after 240s — child produced no output before it was killed

The child wrote NOTHING to stdout or stderr in 240 seconds. That materially narrows hypothesis 1: this is not a slow-but-progressing fetch that merely needs a bigger budget — a page load in progress would produce *something*. Zero bytes across four minutes points at the child hanging BEFORE it does any work: MCP handshake, `--strict-mcp-config` resolution, or the headless Chromium launch.

Start there rather than at the timeout value. Suggested next probe: run the same `claude -p --mcp-config <cfg> --strict-mcp-config ...` by hand with stderr attached to a terminal, and see whether it blocks on the MCP handshake. `linkedin-scraper-mcp --status` drives the server DIRECTLY and returns fine, so the difference is the claude-as-MCP-client layer, not the scraper.

2026-07-31 ROOT-CAUSED — THREE separate causes, stacked. Earlier notes in this task are superseded where they conflict.

CORRECTION to my own earlier note: I wrote that "child produced no output" pointed at the child hanging before doing any work. WRONG. The child was working fine; the PARENT was refusing to read. Also wrong was the premise this task was filed on — the fetch is not too slow. Measured: 98s against a 240s budget.

CAUSE 1 — PIPE-BUFFER DEADLOCK (real, fixed, commit 0cf60779).
call_claude_json_with_mcp piped stdout/stderr, polled try_wait(), and only called wait_with_output() after exit. A pipe holds ~64 KiB; the call emits ~147 KB (2.2x). Child fills buffer -> blocks in write() -> can never exit -> poll never ends. That is why it failed at EXACTLY 240s every time rather than varying, and why zero bytes were seen. Fixed with run_with_timeout(): both pipes drained on threads while polling. Before/after, same URL, unsandboxed: 240s timeout with no output -> 137s with the full response. 3 tests, incl. a 200KB writer that deadlocks without the fix.
  Sub-finding: the timeout path must NOT join the reader threads. Killing the child does not close the pipe if a grandchild holds the write end (Chromium outliving claude) — joining turned a 2s timeout into a 60s stall. Test asserts the bound.
  Also: claude -p waits ~3s for stdin it is never given; now Stdio::null(). 81s across 27 links, paid for nothing.

CAUSE 2 — THE CC SANDBOX BLOCKS IT (environmental, not a code bug).
Running the drain sandboxed reproduces a 240s timeout with no output even WITH the deadlock fix; unsandboxed the same binary reaches the network. Any future verification of this path must run unsandboxed, or it will "reproduce" a bug that is not there. This confounded two earlier runs.

CAUSE 3 — MCP RESULT EXCEEDS THE INLINE TOKEN LIMIT (still open — this is now the blocker).
With 1 and 2 out of the way the fetch SUCCEEDS (100 posts, 58,354 chars) but claude cannot return it inline, so it writes a file and answers in prose. resolve_linkedin_fetch then sees an unexpected shape:
  "The fetch succeeded — 100 posts, 58,354 characters... The MCP result exceeded the inline token limit, so it landed in a file rather than in my context. I wrote the exact requested shape to: .../adrien-taravant-posts.json"
The prompt asks for sections="posts", which returns ALL posts for the author, then Rust fuzzy-matches the one we want downstream (find_matching_post). Fetching ~58KB to keep one post is the design flaw underneath.
FIX DIRECTION (hypothesis, not a decision): have the prompt instruct claude to WRITE the JSON to a caller-supplied temp path and return only that path, then read the file in Rust. Deterministic, sidesteps the token limit entirely, and keeps the existing downstream matching. Alternative: narrow the request so less comes back. NOTE it also litters the cwd — this run left adrien-taravant-posts.json in the worktree (deleted by hand).

tasks.context:
Filed 2026-07-31 from t-2547. ADR-075 decides the trigger and explicitly leaves enforcement to this task, calling out that an unenforced ship rule would be the same advisory-signal artefact the system keeps rediscovering.

TWO PIECES, AND THE SECOND IS THE ONE WITH MEASURED HARM.

PIECE 1 — enforce the trigger. Per ADR-075: any commit touching system/hooks, system/rules, system/agents, or system/cli is promoted to main and deployed on merge to dev. Open question the ADR left: hook, close step, or convention. Prefer a mechanism with a consequence — convention is what produced the state t-2547 was filed about.

PIECE 2 — bootstrap.sh must EXECUTE the binary rebuild, not print it. THIS IS THE DEFECT WITH EVIDENCE.
  bootstrap.sh:931-937  detects brana-cli staleness, echoes a copy-paste cargo command, continues
  bootstrap.sh:946-953  same for brana-mcp (added by t-2378)
  Every `cargo` occurrence in bootstrap.sh is inside a comment or an echo — verified
  `grep -nE "cargo (build|install)" bootstrap.sh` -> lines 27 (comment), 934 (echo), 949 (echo).
So a ship can promote main, run bootstrap, exit 0, look complete, and leave the binary channel stale. The rsync mirror converges by construction; the binary channel converges only if a human reads the output and runs the command.

MEASURED INSTANCE: the live binary was built 2026-07-27T20:30 while the newest system/cli commit was 2026-07-29T10:26. `strings ~/.local/bin/brana | grep -c base_written_at` returned 0 — t-2506's CAS fix, merged with 1265 tests passing, was not in the running binary, so closes were still silently dropping next[] handoff entries. Resolved 2026-07-31T11:46 when someone ran the printed command by hand. The detection worked; only the remedy was optional.

This is the advisory-signal class (ADR-065 D4's unenforced WIP cap, ADR-069 fail-open) sitting INSIDE the deploy path. Printing a remedy and proceeding is the defect, not the mitigation.

DESIGN NOTE — DO NOT JUST ADD `cargo build` TO bootstrap. A release build is slow and bootstrap runs often; making every bootstrap wait on a compile is a different kind of harm and will get worked around. The admissible shapes are (a) rebuild only when the staleness check already fires, (b) fail loudly and refuse to report success while a channel is stale, or (c) split a `--with-binary` deploy path invoked by the ship step specifically. Decide before coding. Note bootstrap.sh:29-31 warns that two binaries resolve through CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT and fall through to the PATH copy if absent — check that interaction before changing install behaviour.

VERIFY-AT-ASSERTION-TIME WARNING FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS: this repo is written by several concurrent sessions and drift readings go stale within the hour. t-2547 produced three withdrawn claims by quoting a `diff -rq` count taken minutes earlier. Re-measure in the same command that uses the result, and report the timestamp. Structural facts (what bootstrap executes) hold; deltas do not.

AC: the trigger is enforced by a mechanism with a consequence, not by convention — and the mechanism is named in ADR-075 or a follow-up note
AC: bootstrap.sh either performs the binary rebuild or fails loudly; it never reports success with a stale binary channel
AC: the chosen shape does not put a release compile in the path of every routine bootstrap run
AC: a deploy-pending indicator derived at read time covers BOTH channels (surface files + binary staleness), per ADR-075
AC: regression test — a stale binary with a clean rsync surface is detected and is not reported as a successful deploy

tasks.context:
Reproduced 2026-07-31 (thebrana, dev).

SCOPE NOTE — read this first. The underlying "sessions cannot tell each other apart" problem is ADR-069 (lane identity), Proposed, with implementation filed as t-2517 (feature spec) / t-2520 / t-2521 / t-2524. This task is deliberately NOT that work. Everything here is a cheap read-side guard that pays off whether or not lane identity lands, and none of it should block on the ADR. If ADR-069 ships first, re-check defect 2 — a real lane key would supersede the recency heuristic proposed below.

DEFECT 1 — build_step trusted over the context that supersedes it.
sitrep showed `t-2568 in_progress, build_step=fix` and recommended `/brana:build`. The same task dump it printed contained "2026-07-31 RESOLVED — ... SHIPPED: b4695c8e + 89d16ac4 ... LIVE VERIFICATION ... AC-2 key verified ... Suite: workspace green, brana-core 690". All three ACs met; the task flipped to completed minutes later. build_step is a lagging field, context is the evidence, and sitrep read the field. Same shape as reading a drift-checker warning as a work order (pattern_verify-the-checkers-baseline-before-applying-its-fix).
Fix: before recommending a resume, scan context for a RESOLVED / SHIPPED / "AC.* verified" marker; when present, downgrade to "needs merge/close" rather than "resume build".

DEFECT 2 — worktree liveness never checked (sitrep/SKILL.md:92).
The cross-check tests only `git branch --merged main`. sitrep listed "worktree already cut" as an ADVANTAGE for t-2568 while another session was committing there (2ffb55ee, 6 min prior; 89d16ac4, 19 min prior). Acting on it means two sessions in one checkout — the t-2216/t-2206 harm class that git-discipline's worktree HARD RULE and the 2026-06-21 field note exist to prevent.
Fix: add a recency probe per worktree — `git log -1 --format=%cr <branch>` — and mark anything under ~30 min CONTENDED, exclude it from "next action", never recommend entering it. Cheap and needs no new state.

DEFECT 3 — the in_progress query pulls full task bodies (sitrep/SKILL.md:96).
`backlog_query(status:"in_progress")` returned 41,781 chars (~13.6k tokens, ~15% of the window) before sitrep produced any output. sitrep renders ~5 fields per task. Measured 2026-07-31 on the same data:
  brana backlog query --status in_progress --output json | jq -r '.[] | "\(.id) | \(.priority)/\(.effort) | \(.build_step // "-") | \(.branch // "-") | \(.subject[0:45])"'
  -> 462 chars. 90x reduction, same table.
Fix: invert SKILL.md:96 for THIS call — projected CLI primary, MCP fallback. The general "prefer MCP" rule in backlog/SKILL.md is not in question; this is a projection concern, not MCP-vs-CLI. Task context fields (Source 3 explicitly wants `.context`) should be fetched per-task on demand, not bulk-loaded for every in_progress task.

DEFECT 4 — close files follow-ups without searching the backlog first.
This is the process defect that produced the duplicates that led here. Evidence: t-2533 (2026-07-28) and t-2576 (2026-07-31) were both filed against the already-open t-2502 by closes that had just hit that bug live and filed straight from the symptom. Both proposed a fix direction t-2502 and ADR-069's Rejected section had already ruled out, so each duplicate was worse than noise — it was misleading guidance sitting in the backlog. Two occurrences in four days on one task.
Fix: in close's follow-up-filing step, run `brana backlog search "<key terms>"` (or backlog_search) before backlog_add, and when a live match exists, append evidence to it instead of filing. Cheap; the search is one call.

RELATED, not duplicated:
- t-2502 — close anchor over/under-reach. Genuinely recurring; do not re-file.
- t-2506 — next[] merge semantics; owns the task_id/handoff-linkage mechanism.
- ADR-069 D3 guards WRITES into a shared checkout; defect 2 guards a READ recommendation. Adjacent, not the same.

FAILURE:
  thread 'commands::doctor::tests::test_expand_env_known_var' panicked at
  crates/brana-cli/src/commands/doctor.rs:822:9
  assertion `left == right` failed
    left:  "/tmp/.tmp7vyehN/.local/bin/brana"
    right: "/tmp/.tmp9FYmGI/.local/bin/brana"

TWO DIFFERENT TEMP DIRS is the tell. The test reads $HOME at doctor.rs:819, then expand_env() reads it again internally; HOME changed between the two reads.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by grep, not inferred): three sibling tests set HOME process-globally to a tempdir while doctor's test is running —
  crates/brana-cli/src/commands/feed.rs:375     unsafe { env::set_var("HOME", tmp.path()) }
  crates/brana-cli/src/commands/session.rs:611  unsafe { env::set_var("HOME", tmp.path()) }
  crates/brana-cli/src/commands/inbox.rs:478    unsafe { env::set_var("HOME", tmp.path()) }
Env vars are per-process, and cargo runs tests in threads within one process, so this is a genuine cross-file race — see pattern_rust-test-per-file-static-mutex-cross-file-race.

1. Make expand_env() take home as a parameter and read std::env::var("HOME") only at the call site. Removes the double-read entirely and matches this codebase's injectable-core convention (resolve_extraction, resolve_linkedin_fetch). Best: kills the race rather than serialising around it.
2. #[serial] on all four tests. brana-cli already uses serial_test in 36 places and its lock is crate-global, so this works — but it is a serialisation band-aid and only holds as long as every future HOME-mutating test remembers to opt in.

DO NOT weaken the assertion — the expectation is correct, the environment is what moves.

tasks.context:
Found 2026-07-31 during a real `/brana:close continue` whose only commit was a tasks.json context append.

VERIFIED ON BOTH SIDES, not inferred from behaviour:
  $ echo ".claude/tasks.json" | close-classify.sh --commit-count 1 --arguments "--continue"  -> INSTANT
  $ echo ".claude/tasks.json" | close-classify.sh --commit-count 1 --arguments ""            -> NANO
close-classify.sh header, lines 16-27: "orientation ... wins over EVERYTHING — including --light/--full/--nano" and "1 commit, <=5 non-code files -> NANO (never queues)". The two rules are individually correct and collide here.
close-snapshot.sh has NO state-file filter (grepped: its only skip paths are missing-binary and unresolvable-range), so it queues whatever range it is handed.

WHY NANO EXISTS (ADR-052 §5): sessions with nothing extractable skip the queue because the extraction overhead exceeds the signal. A tasks.json-only diff is the canonical example — it is machine-written state, not authored work. Forcing INSTANT re-adds exactly the cost NANO was introduced to avoid.

SEVERITY IS LOW AND SHOULD STAY LOW. This is queue noise, not data loss: the nightly cron will find nothing and produce nothing. Worth fixing because a `--continue` mid-session pause is a COMMON way to close, and a tasks.json-only pause is common within it, so the noise is recurring rather than rare. Do not escalate this into a redesign of orientation precedence — orientation-wins is correct for task state and cleanup behaviour, which is what it was introduced for (ADR-053 §1).

FIX DIRECTION (small): keep orientation precedence for task-state/cleanup, but let CONTENT veto the QUEUE specifically — if the changed-file set would classify NANO on its own, skip Step 1b regardless of orientation. Equivalent alternative: give close-snapshot.sh a state-file-only guard so it declines a diff touching nothing but .claude/tasks.json, docs/spec-graph.json and similar generated state. The second is narrower and testable in isolation.

NOT DONE IN THE FINDING SESSION, deliberately: that close skipped its own queue by hand rather than queueing a diff it had just established was noise. Mentioning so the behaviour is not read as the bug recurring.

AC: a --continue close whose only changed files are state files does not queue a snapshot
AC: the same close still writes its handoff and still updates task state (orientation precedence preserved everywhere else)
AC: covered by a case in tests/procedures/test-close-weight-adaptive.sh
tasks.description: close-classify.sh gives orientation absolute precedence, so `--continue` on a session whose only change is .claude/tasks.json classifies INSTANT instead of NANO. INSTANT queues a snapshot; NANO deliberately does not. The nightly extraction cron then receives a JSON state-file diff with nothing extractable in it.

tasks.context:
Observed 2026-07-31 while running /brana:retrospective.

WHAT THE PROCEDURE SAYS (system/skills/retrospective/SKILL.md, Step 5, Pattern branch):
  "Do NOT append to MEMORY.md. Pattern files are findable via ruflo semantic search.
   MEMORY.md entries are added only at explicit human promotion (recurrence >= 3 sessions)."
Step 8 reinforces it: promotion is a separate, user-approved path that also bumps the file's confidence to 0.7.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS: writing pattern_absent-at-runtime-is-not-unmerged_2026-07-31.md took MEMORY.md from 145 to 146 lines with no action of mine — the entry appeared at line 146 with its description already populated. Not a one-off: the tail of MEMORY.md holds several recently-appended patterns from other lanes (pattern_count-by-structural-marker-not-name-exclusion, pattern_worktree-remove-silently-destroys-gitignored-state, pattern_task-notes-are-not-work-state), all in append order rather than the sorted order a rebuild produces.

WHY IT MATTERS — this is a context-budget defect, not a tidiness one. MEMORY.md is the always-loaded tier; it is read into every session. The two-tier design (pattern files findable on demand, MEMORY.md reserved for repeatedly-useful entries) exists so that tier stays small. Auto-indexing collapses the tiers: every one-off observation becomes always-loaded, and the confidence signal (0.5 provisional vs 0.7 promoted) stops corresponding to anything.

DO NOT "FIX" THIS BY DELETING INDEX LINES. A known memory (feedback_memory-indexer-reinflates-removed-entries) records that the indexer re-adds removed entries, so hand-pruning is futile and looks like flapping. The fix belongs in the indexer, not the file.

WHICH SIDE IS WRONG IS AN OPEN QUESTION — decide before implementing. Either (a) the indexer should skip pattern_* until frontmatter shows confidence >= 0.7, honouring the documented gate, or (b) the gate was abandoned deliberately and the skill text is stale, in which case fix the docs and drop Step 8's promotion path. Do not implement (a) without checking whether promotion is still wanted; a skill saying one thing and a hook doing another for months is weak evidence that anyone is using the promotion path.

Adjacent: MEMORY.md was compacted 160 -> 139 lines on 2026-07-31 and is already back to 146 six hours later, which puts the growth rate at roughly one line per pattern written across all lanes.

AC: MEMORY.md indexing behaviour and the retrospective skill agree — one of them changes
AC: if the promotion gate is kept, a freshly written 0.5-confidence pattern does not appear in MEMORY.md
AC: the decision is recorded so the next reader does not re-litigate which side was right
tasks.description: The retrospective skill states that pattern files must NOT be added to MEMORY.md, and that entries are added "only at explicit human promotion (recurrence >= 3 sessions)". An indexer hook appends every newly-written pattern immediately, so the promotion gate never fires and MEMORY.md — the always-loaded tier — grows with unpromoted patterns.

tasks.context:
Found 2026-08-01 on the FIRST live scheduled run after t-2560 re-enabled the timer. Measured, not predicted.

THE RUN: `Drained 10 link(s): 6 completed, 4 left pending, 0 failed.` (Result=success, exit 0.)
The 4 pending are all LinkedIn Ok(None) misses — "post not found in the author's recent feed":
  t-1339 (matiasmolinas), t-1341 (anismiles), t-1342 (midudev), t-1347 (migueloteropedrido)

THE PROBLEM: those 4 are now the FIRST four entries in the pending queue —
  first 8 pending: t-1339 t-1341 t-1342 t-1347 t-1352 t-1353 t-1354 t-1355
so every 4-hourly run spends 4 of its 10 slots re-scraping posts that CANNOT succeed. ADR-070's tier-2 mechanism fetches the author's *recent* feed; a post that has aged out never returns to it. This is not a transient failure that retry fixes — it is permanent, and retry is pure waste (~30-60s of headless Chromium each, 6 runs/day).

IT GETS WORSE MONOTONICALLY: 7 LinkedIn links were attempted this run and 4 missed — a ~57% miss rate. Each future run adds its own misses to the front of the queue. Once accumulated misses reach the cap, new links are starved completely and the job becomes a pure no-op that still burns ~10 minutes of scraping every 4 hours.

WHY LEAVING THEM PENDING WAS RIGHT (do not "fix" this by completing them): t-1366/t-2557 exist because the old script marked links completed without persisting anything. A miss must NOT be silently completed — the content genuinely was not captured. The bug is the unbounded RETRY, not the pending state.

FIX DIRECTIONS (pick one; not a decision):
1. Record attempt state per task (e.g. `link_attempts` + `last_attempt` in context) and have drain-links skip or deprioritise tasks with N failed attempts, so fresh links always get slots. Keeps them visible and re-runnable by hand.
2. Distinguish Ok(None) from a fetch error at the task level — tag a miss as `link-unfetchable` and exclude that tag from the drain query. Cheapest, and makes the population explicit for a human pass.
3. Order the drain queue newest-first so recent posts (still in feed, high success rate) are attempted before aged-out ones. Helps throughput but does not stop the waste.

Option 2 composes well with a periodic manual review of the unfetchable set — those links likely need the public/WebFetch path or manual capture instead.

RELATED: t-2583 (tracking-param slugs) is independent and still open.

AC: a permanently-unfetchable link stops consuming a --cap slot on every run
AC: such links are still discoverable (not silently dropped or falsely completed)
AC: a fresh link cannot be starved by accumulated misses ahead of it in the queue

2026-08-01 DO NOT IMPLEMENT YET — t-2589 may dissolve this.

The audit that followed this task found that every LinkedIn post serves its full body publicly via ld+json articleBody / og:description, above the authwall: 14/15 of the currently-pending links usable at 0.8s each, including all four of the permanent misses that motivated THIS task (t-1339 1615 chars, t-1341 2205, t-1342 283, t-1347 1123).

If t-2589 lands, those links stop being misses at all, and the starvation dynamic this task describes has nothing left to starve on. Building attempt-tracking or an unfetchable tag first would be work aimed at a population that is about to stop existing.

Sequence: decide t-2589 first. Re-scope this task afterwards against the residual miss rate — some genuinely unreachable links will remain (deleted posts, private pages), so a bounded-retry policy may still be wanted, just far smaller and less urgent than P1.

tasks.context:
Found 2026-08-01 verifying t-2560's first scheduled run. Observed directly on link-research-extraction.

THE DISCREPANCY:
  log  ~/.claude/scheduler/logs/link-research-extraction/2026-07-31-183413.log ends with: FAILED (exit code: 1)
  unit systemctl --user show brana-sched-link-research-extraction.service -p Result -p ExecMainStatus
       -> Result=success  ExecMainStatus=0

The runner (~/.claude/scheduler/brana-scheduler-runner.sh) records the job's non-zero exit in its log but does not propagate it, so systemd sees a clean exit.

WHY IT MATTERS: the whole point of the scheduler is unattended operation. Anything that reads unit state — systemctl status, `brana ops status`/`health`, journal alerts — will show green while the job is failing every run. This is the same class as pattern_brana-ops-run-exit-code-lies and pattern_exit-code-is-not-evidence-of-work, but at the layer everything else trusts. I was myself misled by it in this very session: I reported the run as "Result=success, exit 0" while its log said FAILED.

WHAT THE FAILURE ACTUALLY WAS (context, not the bug): 2 of 10 links errored with "LinkedIn session is not usable — run `linkedin-scraper-mcp --login`". Transient — the same two links (t-1344, t-1345) stored fine on the next run, and `--status` reports the session valid now. The run also spanned a laptop suspend (started 18:34, "Finished: 2026-08-01T09:58:03"), which is the likely trigger. The transience is not the point; the invisibility is.

FIX DIRECTION: propagate the job's exit status as the runner's own exit status. Careful about the intended semantics first — drain-links exits 1 when any link failed, which for a capped batch job may be "partial success" rather than "the job broke". Decide deliberately:
  (a) propagate verbatim (simplest, makes systemd honest, but a single bad link marks the run failed), or
  (b) map: all-failed -> non-zero, partial -> zero + a warning surfaced in `brana ops status`.
Do NOT just add `set -e` — that changes behaviour for every job the runner wraps.

AC: a job that exits non-zero causes the unit to report a non-success Result
AC: `brana ops status`/`health` distinguishes a failed run from a clean one for that job
AC: the chosen partial-failure semantics are written down, not implied by the code
AC: regression test covers a wrapped job exiting 1

tasks.context:
Found 2026-08-01 auditing t-2560's first live runs. Measured, not theorised.

THE FINDING: LinkedIn must serve link previews, so a post URL returns the post body in `<script type="application/ld+json">` -> `articleBody`, ABOVE the authwall. No login, no browser, no MCP server. `og:description` carries a second copy, sometimes longer.

SPIKE over all 15 currently-pending link tasks (curl + regex, no deps):
  14/15 usable (>=200 chars), 1 thin, 0 unusable
  15 links in 12.0s total — 0.8s each
Per-link (ld / og / used): t-1339 1615/1615, t-1341 2205/672, t-1342 257/283, t-1347 1123/70,
t-1352 1994/82, t-1353 1998/1999, t-1354 754/754, t-1355 0/56 (thin), t-1356 439/12,
t-1357 2534/97, t-1358 1774/1800, t-1359 1716/1742, t-1360 845/7, t-1361 1515/1515, t-1362 0/896.

TAKE max(articleBody, og:description) — NOT articleBody alone. t-1362 has ld=0/og=896 and t-1342 has ld=257/og=283, so og wins outright on 2 of 15. Each source is individually incomplete.

COMPARISON WITH THE CURRENT TIER 2:
  coverage  ~50% (feed pagination)        vs  15/15 fetched, 14/15 usable
  latency   30-60s per link               vs  0.8s
  auth      one-time login, session expires (2 real failures in run 1, 2026-07-31)  vs  none
  runtime   headless Chromium ~1.3GB      vs  one HTTP GET
  failure   ambiguous "not in recent feed" vs clean HTTP status
All 4 posts tier-2 MISSED return full content publicly (1615/2205/1123/283 chars). On posts tier-2 HIT, JSON-LD often returns MORE than the feed scrape (t-1344 2241, t-1345 1419).
No rate limiting observed: 12 rapid sequential requests, zero 429s.

WHY ADR-070 MISSED THIS: it asked "which MCP tool accepts an arbitrary post URL?", correctly found none, and built an authenticated scraper around get_person_profile. It never asked whether the post URL itself serves the content. Same error shape as t-2568 (claude -p assumed necessary as MCP transport when the server spoke plain JSON-RPC) — the expensive mechanism was built without probing the cheap one.

PROPOSED SHAPE:
1. In fetch_linkedin_content, try the public extract first: GET the post URL, parse ld+json articleBody and og:description, take the longer.
2. If the result is below a threshold (~200 chars), fall back to the existing tier-2 direct-MCP client (t-2568) as enrichment.
3. Keep Ok(None)/Err semantics unchanged: HTTP 404 or an empty extract with no tier-2 result is still Ok(None); a transport failure is still Err.
4. classify_platform keeps routing linkedin separately — this changes what the linkedin branch DOES, not the routing.

DO NOT delete the tier-2 client. It stays as the fallback and is the right implementation for whatever the public path cannot reach; t-2568's work is not wasted, it just stops being the common path.

CAVEATS, stated honestly: n=15, all recent posts from one backlog at one moment. LinkedIn can change its markup — though parsing public preview metadata is markedly less fragile than authenticated DOM scraping. Untested: deleted posts, company pages, very old posts, sustained high-volume bursts. articleBody is the post body only (no comments, though commentCount/comment appear in the LD block).

KNOCK-ON: t-2587 (permanent misses starving the --cap window) largely dissolves if misses stop happening — do not implement its complex attempt-tracking before deciding on this. t-2583 (tracking-param slugs) and t-2588 (runner swallows exit code) are unaffected and remain.

tasks.context:
Found 2026-08-01 during the t-2589 extractor spike, by a burst test rather than by reasoning.

CONCRETE CASE — t-1355:
  stored: https://www.linkedin.com/safety/go/?url=https%3A%2F%2Flnkd%2Ein%2FgmjefVPT&urlhash=Jlev&mt=bB6acGkJrG10EQvi-yH8Q0
  fetched as-is -> HTTP 404, every time, forever
  after unwrapping the `url` query param -> HTTP 200
It was the only non-200 in a 12-URL burst; everything else returned 200. So this is a distinct, narrow class — not general breakage.

WHAT IT IS: LinkedIn rewrites outbound links in post bodies through its click-tracking/safety interstitial. When a link is shared from the mobile app, what lands in the clipboard can be the wrapper rather than the destination. The real target is percent-encoded in the `url` parameter.

FIX: unwrap before fetch. Parse the URL, and if the path contains /safety/go/, replace it with the percent-decoded `url` query parameter. ~4 lines; the spike used:
    q = parse_qs(urlparse(u).query); target = unquote(q.get("url", [u])[0])

NOTE the unwrapped target is usually a further redirect (lnkd.in/...), so the fetch must follow redirects — curl -L equivalent. In the spike the unwrapped t-1355 resolved to only 56 chars of extractable content, so it will likely still be THIN and fall through to whatever the low-content path is (t-2589). Unwrapping makes it fetchable; it does not guarantee it is worth storing.

WHERE: cheapest at fetch time (fetch_url_content, before classify_platform routes it — an unwrapped target is usually NOT linkedin.com and should take tier 1). Better long-term at capture time in the Telegram link-capture path, so tasks.json stores the real URL — but that only helps future captures, so the fetch-time unwrap is needed regardless for the existing backlog.

RELATED: t-2583 (tracking-param slugs) is the same family — captured URLs carrying LinkedIn cruft that the pipeline should normalise. Consider doing both in one URL-normalisation pass: unwrap safety redirects, then strip tracking params, then slugify.

AC: a /safety/go/ URL is unwrapped to its target before fetch
AC: the unwrapped target is routed by its OWN domain, not as linkedin

2026-08-01 RESEARCH (gentle-ai code deep dive) — design decisions settled:
DEVIATE: gentle-ai does NOT execute verification. Its --outcome is a CLI flag the agent supplies (review_artifact.go:44,78) and evidence is caller-supplied bytes that are only SHA-256'd; the only subprocess its review engine spawns is git. Its own threat model says "checksums ... are not authentication" (review-authority-threat-model.md:29). Their receipt means "an agent asserted X over these git trees". OUR mint must execute the test command and hash its own captured stdout+exit code — keep that AC, it is a deliberate deviation.
STEAL (the load-bearing half): the git binding. base_tree/candidate_tree (git tree OIDs from frozen snapshots), paths_digest (domain-separated + length-prefixed, snapshot.go:1313), snapshot identity. These are re-derivable from git at gate time and are what actually catches drift. evidence_hash alone catches nothing — it is only an equality token.
STEAL: three-valued gate result — allow / scope-changed / invalidated / escalated (receipt.go:121-128). "Candidate moved" must be distinct from "approval void" so it routes to recovery, not restart.
STEAL: split pure shape-validation from pure comparison, both with zero I/O; all re-derivation in the caller (validateReceiptStructure + validateDerivedGate; the latter has no repo handle by design).
STEAL: store under `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, not .git — shared across linked worktrees, invisible to git status, never pushed.
STEAL: content-bound finalize journal for idempotency (not a lock) — digest the request, plan revisions, mark published/completed separately; a differing retry is a hard error, the same request resumes.
STEAL: re-check after deciding (re-derive snapshot + re-read authority on the allow path) or the gate is a TOCTOU.
STEAL: canonical JSON, DisallowUnknownFields, reject trailing values; domain-separate and length-prefix every hash input.

2026-08-01 RESEARCH — this task is MORE important than originally scoped. gentle-ai's five gates (post-apply, pre-commit, pre-push, pre-pr, release) are CLI subcommands, NOT git hooks — grep for .git/hooks across its codebase returns nothing. Compliance is procedural, enforced only by agent-facing skill text; nothing physically prevents `git commit`, and an agent that skips `review validate` commits normally. That is pattern_gate-armed-by-the-party-it-constrains present in the reference implementation itself. Our pre-merge hook is therefore the part gentle-ai does NOT have, and the thing that makes a receipt more than advisory. Design consequence: anchor the hook to the merge (involuntary) rather than to any state the committing party opts into writing.
2026-08-02 SPEC FINDING (t-2595) — this task's first AC needs rewording before implementation. "Merge blocked when no valid receipt exists for the branch's task" has no referent at dev->main: promotion is a BATCH carrying every task merged to dev since the last ship. The gate must (1) enumerate task IDs from merge commits on main..dev, (2) require a receipt per task ID rather than per branch, and (3) decide what a merge commit naming no task means — a commit with no task ID is not the same as a task with no receipt, and conflating them fires the gate on the docs/tasks.json churn ADR-075 measured as carrying no deploy footprint. Second finding: candidate_tree will NEVER equal the promotion tip's tree (other tasks merged in between), so the gate checks reachability + paths_digest, never tree equality. A gate built on tree equality passes its own tests and blocks every real ship. Full contract: docs/architecture/features/build-receipts.md.
2026-08-02: `brana receipt validate` ships with distinct exit codes so this hook can branch without parsing stdout — 0 allow / 3 scope-changed / 4 invalidated. tasks.description:
Los subagentes de análisis terminan con status=completed pero sin texto final: lo que llega en la task-notification es vacío o un fragmento intermedio (ej. "Now let's run the actual test suite for AC5."). El análisis se hizo — se ven 60-90k tokens y 14-26 tool_uses en el transcript — pero el informe nunca se emite. Workaround: reanudar con SendMessage pidiendo explícitamente "output your findings NOW as plain text, no further tool calls"; ahí responde completo y bien.

Ocurrió 3 veces en una sola sesión (bemol t-125, 2026-08-01): brana:challenger revisando un spec, brana:build-evaluator evaluando AC, y brana:challenger post-build. Es sistemático.

Hipótesis: el agente agota su presupuesto de turnos y el loop corta cuando el último mensaje es un tool_use, sin dejar turno para la síntesis. Opciones: (a) reservar el último turno para el informe, (b) avisar al agente cuando le queda poco presupuesto, (c) que el harness detecte "terminó en tool_use sin texto" y auto-reanude pidiendo el informe.

Costo: cada corte gasta análisis que hay que rescatar a mano, y si no se nota, el gate se da por cumplido sin veredicto.

tasks.description: The close gate derives its extraction window from LAST_CLOSE — the newest written_at across all epic-keyed session files. When a concurrent session closes LATER than yours, the anchor post-dates your own commits and the window collapses, so your session's work is never queued for the nightly extraction cron. Confirmed live twice: 2026-07-31 (anchor post-dated ALL commits, COMMIT_COUNT=0, false 'read-only session') and 2026-08-02 (a concurrent close at 14:39:57Z post-dated 11 of 13 commits; only the last 2 queued). Proposed fix, sketched by the 2026-07-31 session: when the newest session state post-dates this session's own first commit, anchor on that first commit instead.

tasks.context:

FORMULA (system/scheduler/brana-scheduler, marker block SERVICE-TIMEOUT-BLOCK):
  (maxRetries+1) * (lockWaitSeconds + timeoutSeconds)

tasks.description: brana-scheduler-runner.sh waits up to lockWaitSeconds (default 600) on the per-project flock, but the generated systemd units set TimeoutStartSec=180s. Any job whose project lock is held >180s is killed by systemd as 'start operation timed out' — log contains only the header, no SKIPPED line, no status write; it looks like a hang/mystery failure instead of the designed graceful SKIP. Observed live 2026-08-02 on the first oracle-brana-drift smoke run (thebrana.lock held by another job; unit killed at exactly +180s). Fix options: (a) generate TimeoutStartSec from timeoutSeconds + lockWaitSeconds + margin per job; (b) lower DEFAULTS_LOCK_WAIT below the unit timeout; (c) move the flock wait under the same `timeout` budget as the command. Either way the kill window must not sit between the two configured waits.

Evidence, both writes in one close:

  write 2, base_written_at set -> mode "replace", written 13, state -> 18/8/13 (hand-merged recovery)
Recovery worked and took ~2 min: parse session-history.jsonl with json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode (it is concatenated pretty-printed JSON, not JSONL), take the last row for the epic, union all three lists, re-write with base_written_at = the written_at you just created.

PARSING TRAP worth fixing in the recovery guidance wherever it is documented: an archived row keeps accomplished/learnings/next at TOP level AND also carries a separate 'state' key (key_files/test_status). A recovery script reaching for row.get('state', row) therefore finds 'state' present, looks inside it, and reports 0/0/0 for every archived row — which reads as 'the archive is empty, nothing to recover' when the data is one level up. Cost several minutes before it was spotted.

WHY P1: the close procedure and the proyecto_anita memory both actively RECOMMEND omitting base_written_at on a shared epic file, precisely to get union semantics and avoid deleting other sessions' next[]. That advice is now the data-loss path. Every close following it destroys the prior close's state on that epic.

tasks.description:

The deployed binary has MOVED ON from what t-2549/t-2562 describe — it now emits the documented next{} stats block AND honours base_written_at — but two rows of system/skills/close/phases/session-state.md's merge-semantics table are still false, and both are data-destroying.

Payload with NO base_written_at field at all returned {"next":{"incoming":6,"written":6,"dropped_duplicates":0,"retained_from_existing":0,"mode":"replace-stale"},"warning":null}. An absent token is treated as a STALE token, and replace-stale REPLACES. It did not union, and it did not warn.

Combined effect: on this binary there is NO payload shape that is safe by construction. Passing a matching base with a delta replaces (t-2562 / the documented CAS behaviour). Omitting the base ALSO replaces, via replace-stale. The only protection a caller has is count-before -> write -> count-after -> recover from session-history.jsonl.

tasks.notes:
RESOLVED 2026-08-14 (wave-2 drain beat 4). All 3 ACs met.

(AC1) THE ROTATOR: system/scripts/ruflo-mcp.sh:54-77 — the MCP launcher wrapper, run at every CC session's ruflo MCP start. ruflo_mcp_db_is_healthy() fails → mv memory.db → memory.db.corrupt-$(date +%F) → restore newest backup passing integrity_check. Sole rotator in the system (grep: only this script + its test). "Daily" recurrence = every first MCP launch after corruption OR after a false positive (below).

(AC2) DOES ROTATION DISCARD DATA — YES, three distinct paths, measured:
  a. RESTORE ROLLBACK: live DB replaced by newest healthy backup (daily snapshot, line 83-89) — all writes between snapshot and rotation vanish from live (the 2026-08-02 roll-back-to-07:00 event). Recoverable only by manual salvage from quarantine.
  b. SAME-DAY CLOBBER: quarantine name is date-only — a second rotation the same day mv's OVER the earlier quarantine, destroying it. Proven 2026-08-03: task context records rotations at 09:32 + 09:50, but the surviving .corrupt-2026-08-03 has mtime 12:45 — a third rotation that day; the first two quarantines are gone.
  c. FALSE-POSITIVE ROTATION: .corrupt-2026-08-12 passes PRAGMA integrity_check ("ok") standalone and is row-identical to memory_20260812.db (509=509, anti-join 0) — a HEALTHY DB was rotated. Of 5 quarantines checked: 08-12, 08-03, 08-01, 07-31 check ok standalone; only 08-05 and 08-02 are genuinely malformed. Mechanism: the checker cp's db+wal MID-WRITE (non-atomic copy) — and t-2626's sql.js whole-file 41MB writeFileSync makes a mid-write copy torn by construction — so the COPY fails integrity_check while the real file is fine. The checker manufactures the corruption verdict it then "recovers" from.

(AC3) LINKS: t-2626 owns the write-side root cause (torn whole-file writes — also what makes the checker's copy torn). t-2619 (rotation hardening, in_progress) owns the fix; its context lacked a confirmed mechanism — this finding supplies it: atomic snapshot for the health check (sqlite3 .backup / VACUUM INTO, or flock around the cp), timestamped quarantine names (kill same-day clobber), and quarantine-vs-backup row-diff before restore. Cross-links appended to both tasks.
CORRECTION appended 2026-08-14, after reading t-2619's 08-03 audit (which failed to reproduce checker false-positives under a live WAL writer and invalidated the naive "healthy file discarded" inference): the mechanism in (AC2c) is better stated as CHECK-vs-IN-FLIGHT-WRITE RACE, not a defect inside the checker's copy alone. Sequence: sql.js rewrites the whole 41MB file non-atomically (t-2626); at the instant the health check reads, the on-disk file is GENUINELY torn, so the check fails honestly; mv then moves the inode while the writer's fd keeps writing to it, so the write COMPLETES into the quarantine file — which is why .corrupt-2026-08-12 checks ok today and is row-identical to the backup. The 08-03 audit could not reproduce because it used a live SQLite/WAL writer, not sql.js's writeFileSync pattern. Consequence unchanged: rotation fires on transient in-flight states, quarantines what becomes a healthy file, and rolls live back to the morning backup — recurring data loss whose root cause is t-2626's non-atomic whole-file write. Fix priority follows: t-2626 (atomic write / real sqlite) kills both real corruption and false rotations; t-2619's hardening (timestamped quarantine names, atomic check snapshot, pre-restore row-diff) reduces blast radius meanwhile.

brana_core::util::find_tasks_file() discovers tasks.json via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` and `--show-toplevel` run WITHOUT clearing the git environment. tasks.description:
system/scripts/ruflo-mcp.sh:54-78 runs on EVERY ruflo MCP launch (every new CC session). Two defects compound into a self-sustaining daily data-loss loop.
(1) FALSE POSITIVES: ruflo_mcp_db_is_healthy() (:36-52) copies db, -wal and -shm as three separate non-atomic cp calls while a writer is live, then checkpoints the mismatched copy — manufacturing corruption in the copy. VERIFIED: memory.db.corrupt-2026-07-31 and -08-01 are integrity_check=ok standalone with 4385 and 4332 rows. Two healthy databases discarded for nothing. (2026-08-02 was genuinely damaged, but still holds 4379 readable rows.)
(2) STALE SIDECARS: line 57 moves ONLY memory.db, leaving memory.db-wal/-shm in place; line 72 then copies a backup into memory.db UNDERNEATH the orphaned WAL of the database just rotated away. SQLite replays that WAL onto the fresh backup on next open, immediately re-corrupting it — which guarantees the next session rotates again. Reproduced end-to-end: restore under stale sidecars => 'database disk image is malformed'; same restore with sidecars removed => ok.
(3) NO SALVAGE: mv goes straight to cp of a backup. No .dump attempt. Today .dump still extracts 1393 rows from the rotated file. Note .recover is NOT compiled into this sqlite3 (3.50.6) — use .dump.
MINIMAL FIX (:57): move sidecars with the db, and rm -f the -wal/-shm before the cp at :72. That alone breaks the loop. Then make the health check use 'sqlite3 $db .backup' (atomic, WAL-aware) instead of three cp calls, and .dump-salvage before any mv.

tasks.context:
2026-08-03 VERIFIED EVIDENCE.
- No memory.db-wal or memory.db-shm exist at all -> sql.js never opens the file as a SQLite connection and never uses WAL. PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL in the schema is inert under sql.js.
- CONSEQUENCE: the premise in system/scripts/ruflo-mcp.sh:14-18 ('ruflo uses SQLite WAL mode, which serializes concurrent writes safely ... SQLite WAL is the correct mechanism for concurrent access (t-2085)') is FACTUALLY FALSE for ruflo's own writes. t-2085 removed the flock mutex on that premise. The mutex removal should be revisited on correct facts.
- 8 concurrent ruflo processes observed running simultaneously.
- EMPIRICAL: 6 concurrent 'ruflo memory store' calls -> whole shell OOM-killed (exit 137), 0 of 6 rows landed. 3 concurrent -> one SIGTERMed at the 120s timeout, 2 of 3 landed. Writes can silently fail to land, and a write killed mid-flight is exactly the torn-file corruption source.
- 10 memory.db.corrupt-* files; TWO rotations on 2026-08-03 alone (09:32 and 09:50, the latter quarantining 43.8M).
- Also reframes an earlier finding: 'ruflo memory delete is a silent no-op' may not be a delete bug at all — the delete was likely clobbered by a concurrent whole-file write that still contained the row.
CLEARED as causes (audited): backup-memory.sh --restore and sync-state.sh restore are manual-only, never scheduled; no hook touches ~/.swarm/memory.db; brana Rust CLI is read-only on it; ruflo has NO internal integrity/recovery/reset logic (grep for corrupt|integrity_check|SQLITE_CORRUPT|recover over its dist/src returns nothing).
AC: knowledge writes survive concurrent sessions without silent row loss
AC: a killed writer cannot leave a malformed store
AC: fix does not depend on ruflo changing upstream
2026-08-14 (from t-2615): the torn whole-file write ALSO poisons the rotation health check — ruflo-mcp.sh cp's the db mid-writeFileSync, the copy fails integrity_check, and a healthy DB gets rotated+rolled back to the morning backup (false-positive rotation, e.g. 2026-08-12). Fixing this task removes both real corruption AND the dominant false-positive trigger. Evidence in t-2615 notes.
tasks.description: ROOT CAUSE of the daily store rollback and the .corrupt- files. ruflo uses sql.js (WASM SQLite): it reads the entire memory.db into memory, mutates, and writes the WHOLE file back via non-atomic writeFileSync. Not incremental. db.export() appears at 6+ call sites in @claude-flow/cli/dist/src/memory/memory-initializer.js (:998,:1173,:1365,:1835,:1947,:2295); even a READ rewrites all 41MB because memory_get bumps access_count (:2294). Under concurrency this gives (a) lost update — two writers each read 41MB, last writer wins, silently discarding the other's rows, and (b) torn writes — a writer killed mid-writeFileSync leaves a partially written 41MB file, i.e. a malformed DB, which the next session's health check condemns and rotates. t-2619 fixes the REACTION to corruption; this is the CAUSE.
tasks.notes: Closed 2026-08-14, wave-2 drain beat 6. ROOT CAUSE RESOLVED one level deeper than the task description: sql.js was never supposed to be the writer — it is the FALLBACK. The AgentDB bridge (native better-sqlite3, WAL) crashed on import because pinned @claude-flow/memory 3.0.0-alpha.21 dist/index.js exports ControllerRegistry twice (ESM SyntaxError, live-reproduced: getBridgeFailureReason = "Duplicate export of 'ControllerRegistry'" — t-2757's finding). Failure latches per process → every memory op fell back to sql.js whole-file writeFileSync. Fix: patch-ruflo-memory-dup-export.sh (idempotent backport of the upstream dedupe — keeps shim export, drops legacy dup, keeps INIT_LEVELS; TDD 9/9), wired into ruflo-mcp.sh pre-exec so npm reinstalls self-heal at next MCP launch; applied to the live install immediately. AC1 verified: 6/6 concurrent ruflo memory store landed (isolated store, journal_mode=wal, integrity ok) vs pre-fix baseline 0/6 + OOM. AC2: WAL journal recovery — SIGKILL probes at 1s/2s/3s left integrity ok; a killed writer rolls back, cannot tear the file (vs writeFileSync). AC3: local patch only, no upstream dependency. Consequences: false-positive rotations (t-2615 AC2c) lose their trigger; ruflo-stub-guard agentdb rows updated (bridge now up — re-probe before trusting); -wal/-shm sidecars will reappear next to ~/.swarm/memory.db (expected, healthy).

tasks.description:
brana session epic upsert for a slug with no prior accumulator hit the same class of bug documented for session read (branch main does not match epic convention, falling back to session-state.json), but INSIDE the upsert command itself. Instead of creating an empty accumulator, it populated session-epics/<new-slug>.json with 22 accomplished[] entries copied verbatim from the unrelated orphan session-state.json (a concurrent session's env-hardening/t-2158 work), mislabeled under the new slug. This happened even though the caller passed the correct slug directly and had deliberately bypassed the Tier 0-3 detection cascade (so it is not the same root cause as t-2628 -- that one is about epic-DETECTION being contaminated; this one is a merge-base lookup bug inside the upsert/create path itself, independent of how the slug was chosen).

No data was lost in this instance (env-hardening.json and the orphan session-state.json were both verified untouched; the corrupted file was brand new with sessions_count:1, so deleting it fully restored the correct pre-call state) but a caller who did not sanity-check the result after upsert would have silently believed a fabricated accomplished[] history for their epic.

Repro: create a session-state file (any epic) via brana session write --file, then on branch main (or any branch not matching the epic-slug convention) run brana session epic upsert with a genuinely new slug, --completed empty, --resolved-texts empty array, and inspect the resulting session-epics/<slug>.json -- expect empty/fresh content, actual is a copy of session-state.json (or whichever file the internal fallback resolves).

Suggested fix: the upsert/create path for a brand-new epic slug should never seed its accomplished/next/learnings from a different file found via branch-based fallback resolution -- a new accumulator should start empty, full stop, regardless of what the branch-convention lookup returns.

Source: proyecto_anita close session 2026-08-05, chess-purchase-insights epic. Full writeup: proyecto_anita memory file pattern_close-gate-shared-main-epic-contamination_2026-08-05.md (third variant section).

tasks.description:
Spike (proyecto_anita t-2439, 2026-08-05) confirmed concurrent agent sessions routinely run git add/commit directly against a shared main checkout for bookkeeping commits (chore(tasks), chore(state)) — this is the established convention, not a rule violation (git-discipline.md worktree HARD RULE only covers new-branch creation via checkout -b/switch -c). 11+ distinct pattern variants documented in proyecto_anita memory (2026-06 through 2026-08), 8 occurrences in one day (2026-08-05) alone.

system/hooks/worktree-gate.sh Gate A2 (added 2026-03-16) already attempts to catch this: at git commit time it warns if staged files were not written by the current session (per its own Write/Edit-tool JSONL log). Two structural gaps found:

1. It only tracks files touched via the Write/Edit TOOL, never Bash-invoked writes. .claude/tasks.json -- the single most contended file across concurrent sessions -- is written EXCLUSIVELY via the brana CLI (brana-cli.md: never Read/Write/Edit tasks.json directly), which runs through Bash. So the file most at risk of cross-session absorption is structurally invisible to the one check meant to catch it.
2. It is warn-only, fired at commit time. It cannot prevent the actual race: session A git add followed by session B intervening git commit sweeping A staged files into B unrelated commit. By the time A calls git commit, its files are already gone (absorbed into B earlier commit) -- nothing left to warn about on A side, and B warn (if it fired) does not block.

Recommendation from the spike: an flock-based lock around git add+commit sequences in a shared checkout (e.g. a PreToolUse hook that acquires /tmp/<repo>-main-checkout.lock before any git add/commit/merge targeting the main checkout, released after), closing the timing window directly rather than trying to detect absorption after the fact.

Related: t-2628 (same root symptom, different consumer -- close skill epic-detection Tier2a/2b reads the same contaminated shared git log; that task is about making the READ side robust to contamination, this task is about closing the WRITE-side race itself).
tasks.subject: worktree-gate.sh Gate A2 cannot prevent shared-main-checkout commit races: tasks.json invisible to it, and warn-only cannot close the timing window

tasks.description:
system/skills/close/phases/gate-and-evidence.md Step 1 (CLOSE-ANCHOR-BLOCK, ~line 133-134) computes CHANGED_FILES via `git diff --name-only HEAD~"${COMMIT_COUNT}"..HEAD`. HEAD~N walks first-parent only; when a --no-ff merge commit falls inside the window (every merge-to-dev close does this), first-parent offset N steps back lands on the pre-merge dev tip N merges ago, not N commits of actual session work — the range balloons to include unrelated prior-session commits.

Reproduced 2026-08-06: a 4-commit session (2 branch commits + 2 --no-ff merges) computed COMMIT_COUNT=4 correctly (git log --oneline counts topologically) but HEAD~4..HEAD landed on a commit ~130 commits back, pulling in an entire unrelated t-2630 arc (Rust CLI changes, ADR-077, etc.) into PROPAGATE L1 and doc-drift Step 3b checks.

Step 1b (SNAPSHOT-INVOCATION-BLOCK) already solves this exact problem for its own range via the OLDEST-commit approach: `OLDEST=$(git log --format=%H --since="$LAST_CLOSE" | tail -1)`, then `${OLDEST}^..HEAD`. Step 1's CHANGED_FILES computation should reuse the same safe range instead of HEAD~N.

Symptom of the erroneous range: a close-queue entry with all ~130 files got queued (q-e973dda78d1e8217, dedup_key thebrana:dev:0cf60779..f4219b8a) before being caught and manually marked processed with an explanatory summary to avoid duplicate nightly extraction.
tasks.subject: close gate Step 1 CHANGED_FILES uses HEAD~N (first-parent), over-reaches across merge commits

tasks.description: ~/.claude/hooks/lib/git-helpers.sh extract_cd_prefix_dir() only matches cd X followed by && / ; / || on the SAME line. In a git-worktree session this makes branch-verify.sh check the wrong repo/branch and false-positive cannot stage behavioral files on main even when actually on a feature branch in a worktree. Fix: extend extract_cd_prefix_dir/resolve_lookup_dir to also recognize a cd that is the first line of a multi-line command, newline-terminated, not only && / ; / ||.

tasks.description:
## Symptom

Sitrep on 2026-05-02 missed 5 P0/P1 items that /brana:close had explicitly emitted in its closing report (a checklist with 3 P0 🔴 + 2 P1 🟡 rows: JWT Kapso paste, t-547, t-548/t-554 waiting on Tomás, t-549 webhook API key, t-550 Rule 4 violations).

User flagged it: "es un copy paste del reporte del command close. no se te puede escapar, la gracia es que close y sitrep estén conectados para poder pasar de sesión en sesión."

## Root cause hypotheses

1. **Handoff doc incomplete** — `.claude/session-handoff.md` from the prior close run had a high-level "5 maintenance items" list but did NOT enumerate the new bug task IDs (t-547..t-554) created during that same session's live-test conversation. Either close emitted them to stdout/console only, or wrote them to a different artifact (`brana session write` JSON?) that sitrep didn't read.

2. **Sitrep reads only `.claude/session-handoff.md`** — procedure file at `system/procedures/sitrep.md` Source 4 says: prefer `brana session read --json`, fall back to `brana handoff last` (legacy markdown). I read `.claude/session-handoff.md` directly and never invoked `brana session read --json`. If close wrote structured `next[]` to session JSON, sitrep skipped it.

3. **Sitrep filtered too narrowly when querying backlog** — I queried `backlog_query --tag agent-v4 --status pending --priority P0`, which excluded P1 (t-549, t-550). Should have at minimum surfaced P0+P1 for the active program, OR cross-referenced explicitly against the close-emitted checklist.

## Fix direction

- close MUST persist the full bullet checklist (with task IDs + priority emoji) into a structured field that sitrep is contractually required to read — either `brana session write` JSON `next[]` array OR a top-level `## Open items (from prior close)` section in `.claude/session-handoff.md` that sitrep parses and reproduces verbatim.
- sitrep MUST run `brana session read --json` per its own procedure (currently I shortcut to reading the markdown).
- sitrep query against backlog should include P0+P1 for any tagged program flagged as "active focus" in the handoff, not just P0.
- Add a self-check at the end of sitrep: "did I name every task ID listed in the prior close report? if not, surface delta."

## Repro

Open `.claude/session-handoff.md` from 2026-05-02 close run + the actual close report shown to user (the checklist table with 🔴/🟡). Diff: close report has 5 items with task IDs; handoff markdown has 5 generic maintenance bullets without IDs. The contract is broken at the close-write step.

## Stakes

This breaks the core promise of "close + sitrep make sessions stitch together." Every leaked item is an item the next session re-discovers by accident or never. High-impact for solo operator who relies on these as the memory bridge.
tasks.subject: Bug: close→sitrep handoff loop leaks items between sessions

tasks.context: [migrated from proyecto_anita t-1618, 2026-08-07] 2026-06-20: Discovered during the /brana:close --continue of the platform-ui auth-recovery session while a concurrent identity-commerce session was live in the same repo. Focus was null (cleared, then set to platform-ui-hardening) — neither state changed the routing. Workaround for now: none reliable; content is recoverable via session-state-identity-commerce.json (internal epic field = platform-ui-hardening) + session-history.jsonl archive; sitrep `--all` surfaces it regardless of filename. Related: t-1461 (replace-not-merge same-day). This is brana-system tooling (CLI), tracked here per operator request but belongs to the brana repo.
tasks.description:
`brana session write` resolves the target filename (session-state-{epic}.json) from the auto-detected active epic — the in_progress task's epic — and ignores BOTH the payload's `epic` field and the persistent `brana session epic focus`. When two sessions run in one repo on different epics, the second session's close mis-files.

REPRO (2026-06-20): Session A (this one) did platform-ui-hardening work (t-1466/1467/1472, all completed). Session B (concurrent) drove identity-commerce (t-1601 in_progress). On A's close, `brana session write` with payload `epic:"platform-ui-hardening"` wrote to session-state-IDENTITY-COMMERCE.json (B's epic), because t-1601 was the only in_progress task. Setting `brana session epic focus platform-ui-hardening` BEFORE the write did NOT change the routing — it still wrote identity-commerce.json. So focus is non-functional for `session write` filename resolution.

IMPACT:
1. A's platform-ui handoff lands in the wrong epic file; the correct session-state-platform-ui-hardening.json stays stale (its prior same-day close).
2. The write overwrote the (yesterday) identity-commerce state — archived to session-history.jsonl, but the live file is wrong until Session B closes and rewrites it.
3. Compounds the known replace-not-merge same-day bug (t-1461): two same-epic same-day closes already lose data; cross-epic mis-routing makes it worse.

PROPOSED FIX (pick one, in priority order):
- Honor the payload `epic` field as the authoritative filename key when present (cheapest, correct).
- Else honor `brana session epic focus` (Tier 0) for `session write` routing, not just the close-skill accumulator (Step 9c) — make focus actually bind the write.
- Add a `--epic <slug>` flag to `brana session write` for explicit override.
Also: merge-not-replace when written_at is today (ties into t-1461).
tasks.subject: brana session write mis-routes parallel-session closes — ignores `epic` payload field AND `session epic focus`, keys filename off in_progress-task epic

Si (b) es la conclusión, esto es más una nota de documentación/instrucción a los agentes que un cambio al guard.
