tasks.description:
User concern (2026-08-14): worried that memory pruning sometimes drops important things with no way to recover them, and that pruned entries should be archived somewhere with a pointer left in MEMORY.md, not deleted outright.

Confirmed the actual gap: system/skills/close/phases/metadata-and-memory.md Step 11's classification audit has two branches that call for outright `Delete` with no archive step — entries classified "Derivable" (obtainable via command/file read) or "Historical" (completed, no future value). Both are close-time judgment calls made in a single pass; a misclassified entry is unrecoverable the moment the file is rm'd. (The separate dead-link prepass in the same step is NOT the risk — it only removes index lines whose target file is *already* gone, so no live content is lost there.)

Also relevant, not necessarily in scope: memory-consolidation-scheduled.md's "demote entries no session has read since they were written" and memory-decay-by-non-use.md's recall-hit-count sort don't specify where a demoted/decayed entry lands — same silent-loss shape if "demote" ever resolves to delete rather than move.

Proposed direction (needs a design decision, not prescribing the exact mechanism): before any classification-driven delete, move the source file to an archive location (e.g. `~/.claude/projects/{project}/memory/archive/`) instead of `rm`, and leave a one-line pointer in MEMORY.md (or a dedicated `MEMORY-ARCHIVE.md` index) recording what was archived, when, and why — so nothing vanishes without a trail, even if it's no longer in the always-loaded budget.

Related but distinct — several existing pending tasks (t-2073, t-2098, t-1843, t-2672, t-2071, t-1820) implement the *current*, delete-based pruning mechanism to bring MEMORY.md under its line cap. This task is about changing that mechanism's safety property, not about line-count reduction — file this first if the archive convention should land before those consolidation passes run again, otherwise they'll keep exercising the delete-only path.
tasks.subject: Memory pruning can silently discard content — archive-then-delete with a MEMORY.md pointer instead of hard-delete

tasks.context:
2026-08-17: Disparado por un incidente en vivo durante /brana:close --finish en el proyecto somos_mirada. Un session write SIN campo epic en el payload (usuario había elegido explícitamente skip — sin epic en el picker Tier 3) igual se enrutó a session-state-lifecycle-workflows.json vía el marcador de foco persistente (Tier 0), porque la corroboración solo se aplica cuando SI hay un TIER0_SLUG que contradice los commits de la sesión — no cubre el caso de epic explícitamente vacío pero el marcador persistente igual gana. Al ser un write cross-day, hizo replace-stale completo y borró next[] abiertos (t-159, t-175, un ítem de mantenimiento) de una sesión no relacionada (Vero SM / lifecycle-workflows). Detectado y corregido en la misma sesión de cierre (restaurado vía write corrector con base_written_at) — nada se perdió, pero fue una detección manual, no una protección estructural.

Evidencia de que esto no es un caso aislado: close/phases/session-state.md documenta ~8 incidentes/parches previos sobre el mismo mecanismo, todos con la firma un slug se enruta mal y session write hace replace no merge sobre estado ajeno: t-2263 (Tier 2a sin corroboración clobbereó epic orbit no relacionado), t-2480 (mismo over-reach en el acumulador COMPLETED), t-2506 (same-day merge semantics, causa raíz del CAS token), t-2603 (divergencia scoped vs unscoped, exclusión silenciosa de epics), t-2618 (gate de corroboración para Tier 0 — el mismo tier que falló hoy), t-2674 (el más grave: la tabla de contrato documentado NO es garantía, 2 wipes en vivo bajo condiciones contradictorias, causa raíz nunca identificada), t-2768 y t-2784 (ventana flat -20 sigue fallando en bajo commit-count o alta concurrencia).

Preguntas a responder: 1) Qué valor real aporta (routing de handoffs, continuidad cross-day en sitrep) vs costo (>2000 líneas de lógica defensiva, ~8 incidentes documentados, uno en vivo hoy). 2) El caso de uso real se podría resolver más simple — epic explícito y obligatorio en el payload, sin fallback silencioso a marcador global? 3) El fallback al marcador persistente es la causa raíz recurrente? Si se eliminara (exigir epic explícito o dejarlo huérfano), qué se rompe? 4) Recomendación final: mantener / simplificar (qué cortar) / eliminar y reemplazar por qué.

Nota: de los 8 incidentes citados, t-2480, t-2506 y t-2674 siguen abiertos (pending/in_progress) — son parches puntuales al mismo mecanismo, en curso en paralelo. Este audit es upstream de esos parches (decide si el mecanismo debe existir en su forma actual), no bloqueante ni bloqueado por ellos — pero coordinar antes de proponer eliminar/rediseñar para no pisar ese trabajo.

tasks.description: Implement Metric 1 (ADR-083): wire START/CLOSE effort markers into build.md's LOAD and CLOSE steps, keyed by task_id, for all effort sizes. acceptance_criteria: Audit: read always-use-build-framework.md, start.md, and build.md's CLASSIFY phase as they exist today

tasks.context:
The 4 criteria used (session 2026-08-17, proyecto_anita anita-envios drain):
1. Multiple viable designs exist -> full build earns its keep (adversarial pass catches a bad structural choice before code exists). If the pattern is already established by sibling code (e.g. t-2704's error_log->gate_runs, admin_audit_logs already used identically elsewhere for t-2705), there's nothing to challenge -- 'propose 3 approaches' is theater over a copy-adjacent pattern.
2. Blast radius / production risk -> worth the extra scrutiny regardless of design ambiguity (e.g. a task that fires real sends, or handles a server-side API key).
3. Compounding risk across a dependency chain -> challenge once at the HEAD of a multi-task chain (where later tasks build on the first one's shape/AST/schema), not on every link.
4. UI/UX -> if the user has already asked to be looped in directly on UI decisions via live conversation, that conversation IS the challenge -- running the skill's CHALLENGE phase on top is redundant.

Applied retrospectively, this matched what actually happened for the first two tasks completed that session (t-2704, t-2705): no real design decision existed to challenge, just an existing pattern extended correctly -- confirming the heuristic wasn't just post-hoc rationalization for skipping ceremony.

OPEN QUESTION for this task: should start.md's step 4 (auto-classify strategy) or build.md's CLASSIFY step incorporate a similar auto-assignment -- e.g. a lightweight heuristic (grep for: does this task extend an existing pattern already used elsewhere in the codebase? does it touch a known-sensitive surface -- payments, sends, credentials, auth, migrations? is it the first task in a chain of blocked_by/parent-linked siblings?) that suggests 'full build' vs 'lighter flow' with a confidence score, presented via AskUserQuestion for a quick confirm/override rather than either (a) rigidly forcing full ceremony on every task regardless of size, or (b) leaving each session to reinvent the gating logic from scratch. Needs to preserve the 'no silent skip' spirit of the original rule (the exceptions must be visible/auditable, not a quiet default) while reducing the actual friction on genuinely bounded, pattern-following S/M tasks.

Not a decision to make unilaterally in this task -- surface options (e.g. as a proposed addition to always-use-build-framework.md with an explicit opt-out clause + audit trail, or as a new step in start.md's Step 4) and get a human call before changing the standing rule.
tasks.description: During a 16-task backlog-drain session in proyecto_anita (anita-envios epic, t-2704..t-2658 etc.), the standing rule 'always-use-build-framework' (no exceptions for S-effort) collided with an explicit user authorization for a faster autonomous mode. Resolved ad-hoc, mid-session, with a 4-criterion heuristic gating full /brana:build vs a lighter TDD-only flow (worktree -> test-first -> typecheck -> full suite -> merge --no-ff -> mark done, skipping CHALLENGE/PROPOSE/SPECIFY).

tasks.description:
system/skills/close/phases/session-state.md documents: "next[] with stale/absent base_written_at → union + warning". Live-reproduced 2026-08-13 during a /brana:close --finish on proyecto_anita, epic "anita-envios": called `brana session write` with NO base_written_at field in the payload at all. Response: {"mode":"replace","warning":null} — not "union", no warning. The write silently discarded 5 legitimate next[] items from a same-day, ~13-hour-earlier session (t-1884 go-live checklist, t-2663, t-2664, t-2575, t-2571), keeping only the 3 new items from this write.

Data loss caught and manually corrected by recovering the prior next[] from system/state/.../memory/session-history.jsonl (archive), re-running the write with the recovered items unioned in plus an explicit base_written_at. The archive saved this — a session without archive access would have silently lost the 5 items with no error signal anywhere.

CORROBORATING PRIOR INCIDENT (found after filing, via ~/.claude/projects/{project}/memory/pattern_session-write-replace-wipes-prior-next_2026-08-11.md — should have been checked BEFORE filing, not after): 2026-08-11, same "anita-envios" epic, a DIFFERENT trigger — that time base_written_at WAS correctly matched/provided, and it STILL replaced wholesale (retained_from_existing: 0), destroying 5 then-live items (t-1884, t-2605, an untracked item, plus 2 legitimately-completed ones). So there are now two independent, live-reproduced incidents two days apart with two different trigger conditions (omitted base_written_at vs. correctly-matching base_written_at) producing the identical destructive outcome (wholesale replace, zero retained, no warning signal in the response). This strongly suggests "mode: replace" ALWAYS discards next[] wholesale regardless of how the call is made, and the documented "union on absent/stale base" fallback either never worked or regressed.

Either the CLI's actual behavior needs to change to match the documented union-on-absent-base contract, or the doc needs to be corrected to say "next[] write is fundamentally replace-only, caller must always read-modify-write" (in which case close/phases/session-state.md Step 9b's CAS-token framing is misleading — it implies base_written_at is only needed to WITHDRAW an item, when in practice the write is destructive by default regardless of the token).

tasks.context: Surfaced by the t-2945 Challenger gate (iteration 2, 2026-08-18) as a severity-4 finding: the ADR-070 youtube tier stores full raw transcripts in the knowledge namespace, but knowledge-vector-sync's embedder has no chunking, so semantic search on long entries silently degrades to matching only the embedded prefix. Not blocking t-2945 (ADR documents the limitation explicitly); this task is the real fix.
tasks.description:
knowledge-vector-sync (t-2620, system/cli/rust/crates/brana-core/src/vector.rs, RufloEmbedder) embeds the full stored value of every knowledge:url:<slug> entry through ruflo's all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384d, ~256-token max sequence length) with no chunking anywhere in vector.rs. For short values (LLM-summarized insights via extract_insight) this was always within the model's window. t-2945 (ADR-070 youtube tier) is the first write path to store long raw text directly (measured 152,208 chars / one real transcript) -- the embed call will silently truncate to the model's context window, so semantic search on that entry only matches its opening content. Exact-key recall and full-text storage are unaffected; this is specifically a semantic-search quality gap.

Fix: chunk long values before embedding (or embed multiple windows and store multiple vectors per key, RRF-merged at query time) inside vector.rs / knowledge-vector-sync -- benefits any future long-content tier, not youtube-specific. Until this lands, t-2945's ADR documents the degraded-search limitation explicitly rather than silently.
tasks.subject: knowledge-vector-sync: chunked/multi-vector embedding for long-content entries

tasks.context: Discovered 2026-08-17 during t-2921 rung-2 verify stage (ADR-082 judge panel). brana-cli/src/commands/decisions.rs's append-only JSONL write (writeln!(file, "{}", entry), entry: serde_json::Value formatted via Display -- multiple write() syscalls, not one) has never been concurrency-tested; its own test module is single-threaded. POSIX O_APPEND atomicity is per-syscall, so a multi-syscall write can interleave with a concurrent writer and corrupt the file. Cited as a precedent by docs/architecture/features/time-tracking-metric-1.md's data-store design (t-2921/t-2922), which mandates a single pre-serialized write_all per line specifically to avoid this class of bug for the NEW code -- but the EXISTING decisions.rs code still has the unverified assumption. Needs: a concurrent-writer stress test (queue.rs-shaped: N threads appending decision entries to the same store, assert no corrupted/interleaved lines) to either confirm it's safe in practice (small JSON lines under PIPE_BUF may make this a non-issue) or fix it to match the same single-write_all pattern.
tasks.subject: Concurrency-test decisions.rs's writeln! append pattern (never stress-tested)

tasks.description:

Documentation (pattern_absolute-path-edits-bypass-worktree-cwd in auto memory) has not prevented recurrence across two separate sessions.

Proposed fix: a PreToolUse hook on Edit/Write that, when a worktree is active for the session (detectable via `git worktree list` matching the session's known branch, or explicit session state), rejects or warns on any file_path not rooted under that worktree's path. Needs design: how to detect "the active worktree" reliably (branch-keyed session state already exists per project_branch-keyed-sessions memory), and whether warn vs. hard-block is right (a legitimate cross-worktree edit, e.g. reverting a stray change in main, should still be possible with explicit intent).

tasks.description:
brana session write --file routes the write to a session-state-{epic}.json that does NOT match the epic field explicitly set in the payload JSON, and the target file gets replaced (mode: replace-stale in the response) rather than safely unioned, despite the write carrying a base_written_at that was stale relative to the target file it actually landed in.

Live repro (proyecto_anita, 2026-08-20, close --finish orientation):
1. Read current agent-epic session state via `brana session read --all --json`, captured its written_at as base_written_at.
2. Built a payload with "epic": "agent" explicitly set, next[] composed as read+merge of the agent epic's existing 62 items (minus one completed task, plus one new item) per the documented read+merge discipline.
3. Called `brana session write --file <payload>`.
4. Response: {"ok":true,"path":".../session-state-anita-envios.json","next":{"incoming":55,"written":55,"dropped_duplicates":0,"retained_from_existing":0,"mode":"replace-stale"}} — wrote to the ANITA-ENVIOS epic file, not agent. Also: 55 written vs 62 sent, dropped_duplicates:0, no accounting for the 7-item discrepancy.
5. Post-write inspection: the agent epic's own session-state file was confirmed UNCHANGED (same written_at as before the write attempt) — the payload's epic field was silently ignored for write routing.
6. A subsequent read of anita-envios' session-state moments later showed a session_label that did NOT match the payload sent (no trace of it, not even via the documented ' | ' concatenation), and a next[] list containing at least 5 items cross-checked as originating from the agent-epic content sent in the payload — suggesting either (a) a second concurrent write landed on anita-envios within seconds and read-merged over content that briefly included the misrouted write, or (b) some other race. Root cause of the routing mismatch itself was not determined in-session — no CLI source access from that session.

Why this matters: this is a NEW failure trigger for the class already tracked at t-2674 (session write replace/union behavior root cause, unfixed) — prior documented triggers were (a) a correctly-matching base_written_at still destructively replacing, and (b) base_written_at omitted entirely. This adds a THIRD: an explicit epic field in the payload being ignored for routing, landing content on the wrong epic's file entirely — cross-epic contamination, not just same-epic history loss, which is a materially worse failure mode.

Suggested angles to improve (not decided, needs CLI source investigation):
- Confirm what brana session write --file actually uses for write-target routing (epic field in payload? current git branch? a focus/initiative marker? some precedence order that silently falls through when a check fails?) — the existing doc claim ("payload epic routes it", close skill's session-state.md Step 9 routing note) was directly contradicted by this repro.
- If routing legitimately depends on something other than the payload's epic field, the CLI should either honor an explicit epic field when present (fail loud if it can't resolve it), or the close skill's documentation needs correcting to match actual behavior — right now the two disagree.
- Consider making a requested-vs-resolved epic mismatch a hard error or at minimum a visible warning field in the write response, rather than silently proceeding.
- The 55-vs-62 incoming/written discrepancy with dropped_duplicates:0 suggests a second silent filtering/dedup path not reflected in the response schema — worth surfacing.

Related: t-2674 (same underlying CLI area, different trigger conditions — cross-link, not a duplicate given the different failure shape: wrong-epic-file vs same-epic replace/union). Project memory pattern in proyecto_anita: pattern_session-write-replace-wipes-prior-next_2026-08-11.

Impact assessed as non-critical for now: no user-facing or production code was affected (internal session-handoff bookkeeping only), and the two proyecto_anita epic files involved (agent, anita-envios) were confirmed not to have lost anything essential — the session's actual substantive record (task t-2804) is independent of this mechanism. Filed to close the gap before the next close hits the same surprise.

tasks.description:
Live-confirmed 2026-08-20 (t-2997 close): this session's 4 own commits were ~6.5h old by close time. The CLOSE-ANCHOR-BLOCK's SESSION_EPICS computation uses a flat `git log --since=\"6 hours ago\"` to find task IDs and resolve their epic — with commits just outside that window, SESSION_EPICS resolved empty, so LAST_CLOSE fell back to selecting the max written_at among \"(orphan)\"-epic session-state files only, landing on a 3-week-stale file (2026-07-31T20:09:57). COMMIT_COUNT computed as 679 (the entire repo history since that stale anchor) instead of the session's actual 4 commits. tasks.context:
Surfaced 2026-08-22 during the-brana-guide.md's L3.1 ring-table walk (t-2490). Source: docs/research/2026-08-18-pocock-methodology-synthesis.md §1/§4 N2 (worktree thebrana-t-2837) — a third-party comparison piece reports Pocock argues refactoring belongs in code review, not the red-green-refactor loop. That doc's own recommendation: "INVESTIGATE, don't adopt blind — genuine disagreement with current practice, worth a small spike/trial on 2-3 tasks before deciding, not silent inheritance either way."

Operator decision 2026-08-22: run this as its own spike (not folded blindly into the ring table), matching the same probe-before-build discipline already used for the JUDGE-panel decision (loop-task-multiagent.md Rounds 4-5b: measure before build, no adoption on priors).

TRIAL DESIGN (draft, refine at spike start): pick 2-3 real S/M tasks. For each, run TDD with refactor deliberately deferred out of the inline loop (commit red, commit green, stop — no refactor pass) and let the refactor happen explicitly at the code-review/challenger stage instead. Compare against the current inline-refactor baseline on: (a) does deferred refactor actually happen, or does it get skipped/forgotten once the immediate task feels "done"; (b) does review-stage refactor still have enough context to be safe (the reviewer isn't the implementer — this is Pocock's own stated benefit, a second pair of eyes, but also a risk: the sequential-handoff context-loss finding from docs/research/2026-08-14-multiagent-orchestration-lessons.md may apply here too); (c) net time/cost vs the current inline approach.

Depends on: whether brana's build-loop's JUDGE/CLOSE stage can actually absorb a refactor pass (does challenger/evaluator have room to do structural cleanup, or are they scoped to review-only today — check system/skills/build/phases/verify-gates.md and _shared/challenger-gate.md before designing the trial).

AC: trial run on 2-3 real tasks, results compared against inline-refactor baseline on the three axes above
AC: explicit verdict recorded — adopt the split, keep brana's inline model, or hybrid — with evidence, not priors
AC: if adopted, L3.1's ring table (the-brana-guide.md) updated to move refactor from Micro's beat-unit to Beat-ring's Judge column; if rejected, the-brana-guide.md notes the rejection with evidence so it isn't re-litigated blind later
2026-08-22 (L3.2 walk, t-2490): PRIOR ART — ADR-061 §4 invariant 3 (Accepted 2026-06-21) already places refactor OUTSIDE the /goal iterate span (span = red→green only; refactor capped/optional, outside the done-predicate). So brana's accepted position is already halfway to Pocock's refactor-in-review. Sharpen the spike's question accordingly: not 'inside vs outside the TDD loop' (already outside the /goal span) but WHO runs the refactor pass and WHEN — the builder right after green in the same context (Micro ring), or the reviewer at the Beat-ring valve (Pocock's practice). Trial design should compare those two, not the strawman of inline-refactor-inside-/goal. Cite ADR-061 §4 in the verdict either way.

tasks.description:
Live-confirmed 2026-08-23: ran `brana knowledge channel-backfill` against a real channel (https://www.youtube.com/@MattPocockAI), which correctly enumerated and queued 2 videos (t-3024, t-3025). `brana knowledge drain-links --platform youtube` then failed both with yt-dlp's "Sign in to confirm you're not a bot" error, even after (1) updating yt-dlp from 2026.03.17 to 2026.08.19 via pipx, and (2) installing a JS runtime (deno) so yt-dlp's PO-token challenge solver could run. Deno got further (attempted the challenge) but still failed with "Missing required Visitor Data" / PO token issues.

Confirmed the actual fix works: `yt-dlp --cookies-from-browser chrome <url>` succeeds against the same video (verified live, lists caption tracks successfully) — YouTube's current anti-bot measures effectively require an authenticated session for reliable extraction, not just a fresh yt-dlp + JS runtime.

Root cause in code: `build_yt_dlp_caption_args()` in system/cli/rust/crates/brana-core/src/knowledge_pipeline.rs (~line 1741) builds a fixed, pure argv with no cookie/auth passthrough of any kind — no CLI flag exists on `drain-links` or `channel-backfill` to supply `--cookies-from-browser <browser>` or `--cookies <file>` to the underlying yt-dlp call.

After pipx inject yt-dlp secretstorage: 'Item does not exist!' (Chrome Safe Storage key not in GNOME keyring); chrome+basictext: 'cannot decrypt v11 cookies'. tasks.description: brana-core/src/ruflo.rs ruflo_memory_store passes the whole value as an argv `--value` arg. A long transcript (t-3063, "Building a REAL feature with Claude Code", ~1h) exceeds the single-arg limit → `failed to spawn ruflo memory store: Argument list too long (os error 7)`. drain-links leaves the task pending and retries forever. Root cause: value transported via argv. Fix: pass value via stdin or a temp file (check ruflo memory store for --file/stdin support; else chunk or truncate with explicit marker). Class: any raw-transcript store (t-2950 path), not just YouTube.
tasks.notes: Retrospective: root cause was Linux's per-argv-string MAX_ARG_STRLEN (131072 bytes) — a distinct, tighter constraint than the aggregate ARG_MAX (2MB) that the task description assumed. Confirmed the CLI's preferred fix ("pass via stdin/temp file") was not available upstream (verified against installed @claude-flow/cli source: value comes only from ctx.flags.value/ctx.args[0], no stdin/--file path) before implementing the spec's named fallback (truncate with explicit marker). Fix lives in ruflo_memory_store itself, protecting every current/future caller, not just process-url. Docs step skipped per docs/SKILL.md rule 5 (bug fixes skip docs entirely) and t-3149 (the close.md step-6 table references a nonexistent /brana:docs "update" subcommand — pre-existing drift, not touched here). Pattern + field note stored to ruflo memory (pattern:thebrana:argv-e2big-max-arg-strlen, field-note:thebrana:ruflo-cli-no-stdin-file-value). 4 sibling tasks opened: t-3152, t-3153, t-3154, t-3155.

challenger agent type lacks SendMessage — cannot reply as teammate
tasks.description: brana:challenger agent definition has no SendMessage tool, so spawning it as a teammate expecting a direct reply deadlocks. Either grant it SendMessage or fix call sites to use the standard completion path instead.
tasks.context:
The brana:challenger agent definition's tool list (Read, Glob, Grep, Write, Edit) has no SendMessage — confirmed via the runtime agent-type listing (system prompt "Available agent types" enumerates its tools). When challenger is spawned as a long-lived "teammate" (e.g. named `t2841-challenger`) expecting to report findings back via SendMessage, it is structurally unable to reply — waiting on it stalls forever regardless of timeout. Observed in session 2026-08-23: fell back to spawning a fresh challenger agent via the standard completion path (return value / final text) instead of waiting for a SendMessage reply.

Fix direction: either (a) add SendMessage to the challenger agent's tool list if it is meant to be addressable as a long-running teammate, or (b) document/enforce that challenger is a one-shot completion-path agent only and never spawn it expecting a SendMessage reply (fix the orchestration call site(s) instead). Prefer (b) unless there's a real need for challenger to hold a multi-turn conversation as a teammate — adding SendMessage to a review-only agent's tool list expands its blast radius for no clear benefit.

tasks.subject: Wire YouTube transcripts into the Tier1/2/3 knowledge-pipeline (dimension-doc synthesis)
tasks.description:
brana knowledge process (Tier1 relevance score -> Tier2 cluster -> Tier3 LLM-drafted dimension doc) is a fully separate system from process-url/drain-links/channel-backfill: it reads PipelineState (~/.swarm/knowledge-pipeline-state.json), populated only by `brana knowledge ingest` from LinkedIn/GitHub/Substack/arxiv URLs. YouTube transcripts drained via drain-links go straight into ruflo memory (knowledge:url:* keys, namespace "knowledge") and never touch PipelineState — there is no code path connecting the two. UrlEntry.fetched_content exists generically but is populated by nothing; its doc comment points at t-1144 (LinkedIn-only, gated on the LinkedIn pipeline's own first full cycle, unrelated to YouTube).

Motivation: raw transcripts rank poorly in semantic search against short, topically-tight content (live-tested 2026-08-23: a video's own title phrase surfaced Reddit/HN feed items above the video itself). Synthesized dimension docs would be far more findable.

Open design questions for SPECIFY (none resolved yet):
1. Do Tier1's relevance-scoring prompt and Tier2's clustering logic work sensibly against transcript-length content, or do they assume short LinkedIn-post-length input and need a YouTube-specific variant?
2. How does a YouTube UrlEntry get created — does channel-backfill/drain-links start writing into PipelineState in addition to (or instead of) ruflo memory, or does a separate `brana knowledge queue-for-dimensions` step read from the already-stored knowledge:url:* keys?
3. Does the existing draft cap (10) and promotion review flow apply unchanged, or does transcript volume need its own cap?
4. Relationship to t-1144 (LinkedIn v2 full-fetch) -- confirm this is a genuinely separate task, not accidentally reopening that gate.
tasks.context: 2026-08-23: user asked to add "enrichment" (dimension-doc synthesis) as an automatic step after channel-backfill/drain-links, following a Matt Pocock (@mattpocockuk) YouTube backfill session (t-3097 area). Investigation found no existing wiring; user chose to spec this properly rather than hack a quick hook.

tasks.subject: knowledge_pipeline.rs LLM prompt calls hit E2BIG on unbounded fetched content (t-3096 sibling)
tasks.description: extract_insight()/extraction_prompt(content) in system/cli/rust/crates/brana-core/src/knowledge_pipeline.rs (~lines 2481-2493) embeds the full unbounded fetched URL content into a prompt string, which is then passed whole via argv at 3 subprocess spawn sites: call_gemini_json (line ~2618-2620, Command::new(bin).arg("-p").arg(prompt)), call_claude_json (line ~2704-2712/2769-2770, via build_claude_args), and call_claude_text (line ~2824-2825). Long articles or transcript pages routinely exceed 100KB, hitting the same Linux MAX_ARG_STRLEN (131072 bytes) E2BIG failure that t-3096 fixed in ruflo_memory_store. Fix should apply the same class of guard (truncate with explicit marker before building the argv prompt, or find a stdin-capable invocation path for these CLIs) at the prompt-construction boundary in knowledge_pipeline.rs.
tasks.context: 2026-08-23: surfaced by t-3096's rung-1 second-variant finder (challenger gate, severity 4). Same class as t-3096 (E2BIG via unbounded argv value to a subprocess) but in a different subsystem (LLM insight extraction, not ruflo memory store) — out of scope for t-3096's S sizing, tracked separately per no-patches-root-cause discipline.

tasks.subject: agy_delegate MCP tool hits E2BIG on large task/context payloads via argv (t-3096 sibling)
tasks.description: build_prompt(task, context, output_format) in system/cli/rust/crates/brana-mcp/src/tools/agy_delegate.rs (~lines 58-77, 174-183, 236-245) concatenates the MCP tool's free-form task/context into one uncapped prompt string, then invoke_agy_with_bin does Command::new(bin).arg("-p").arg(prompt). This is the primary system-wide agy/Gemini delegation surface (delegation-routing.md) — any sufficiently large task/context payload (a diff, a transcript, a research corpus) hits the same Linux MAX_ARG_STRLEN (131072 bytes) E2BIG failure that t-3096 fixed in ruflo_memory_store. Fix should apply the same class of guard at the prompt-construction boundary, or investigate whether the agy CLI supports stdin/file input for its -p prompt.
tasks.context: 2026-08-23: surfaced by t-3096's rung-1 second-variant finder (challenger gate, severity 4). Same class as t-3096 (E2BIG via unbounded argv value to a subprocess) but in a different subsystem (agy delegation, not ruflo memory store) — out of scope for t-3096's S sizing, tracked separately per no-patches-root-cause discipline. Higher blast radius than t-3096: agy_delegate is the sanctioned cross-model delegation path per delegation-routing.md.

tasks.subject: Shell hooks call $CF memory store -v with unbounded value, bypassing t-3096's Rust fix (t-3096 sibling)
tasks.description: t-3096 guarded ruflo_memory_store (the Rust wrapper) against E2BIG, but several bash callers invoke $CF/ruflo memory store directly and are untouched by that fix: system/hooks/session-end-persist.sh (lines 74, 106 — $VALUE is a jq-compacted session summary that scales with session length, runs unconditionally on every session close, highest exposure), system/scripts/memory-store.sh (lines 23-27, generic eval'd -v wrapper with no size bound, an ad-hoc entry point any caller can use), and lower-risk system/hooks/post-tool-use-failure.sh (144-148) and system/hooks/post-sale.sh (81-86) where payload is currently bounded by construction. Fix should add a shared shell helper (byte-length check + truncate-with-marker, mirroring ruflo.rs's truncate_utf8_safe/MAX_ARGV_VALUE_BYTES) and wire it into these call sites, or route them all through a single guarded entry point instead of duplicating the check.
tasks.context: 2026-08-23: surfaced by t-3096's rung-1 second-variant finder (challenger gate, severity 4 for session-end-persist.sh; severity 3 for memory-store.sh; severity 2 for post-tool-use-failure.sh/post-sale.sh). Same class as t-3096 but the shell-side callers were never in scope for the Rust fix — they call the ruflo CLI directly, not through ruflo_memory_store. Out of scope for t-3096's S sizing, tracked separately per no-patches-root-cause discipline.

tasks.subject: Extend t-3096's argv-truncation guard to ruflo.rs's remaining unguarded params (t-3096 sibling)
tasks.description: t-3096 guarded only ruflo_memory_store's --value param. The primary challenger (same gate) flagged that ruflo_memory_search_raw's -q query param (system/cli/rust/crates/brana-core/src/ruflo.rs ~lines 122-133) shares the identical Command::args()/MAX_ARG_STRLEN transport and ceiling, untouched; and that ruflo_memory_store's own key/--tags params (lines 246, 254-257) are also argv-transported without a length guard (key is a bounded URL slug — low risk; tags generation not fully traced). Separately, vector.rs's RufloEmbedder::embed -t text param (~lines 371-372) shares the same mechanism. All are currently low-reachability (short queries/slugs/tags in practice today) — this is a hardening/consistency task, not an active bug, so lower priority than the other t-3096 siblings.
